title: One-Touch Cook Button
new_elements: One-Touch Cook Button (Single large button replaces timer and power knobs.); Auto-cook any food (Uses sensors to choose time and power automatically.)
rationale: A single button removes all settings decisions, so no learning curve is needed.
judge_comment: Directly removes settings decisions, though one-button auto-cook with sensors already exists in part and is not very radical.

title: Auto-Sensing Door Open
new_elements: Proximity Door Sensor (Detects hand near door and releases latch automatically.); Hands-free door opening (Door opens without pushing a button or pulling a handle.)
rationale: Removing the door-release button makes opening obvious and effortless.
judge_comment: Easy to build and mildly helpful for door opening, but it addresses only a small part of operation and could open the door accidentally.

title: Voice-Only Control
new_elements: Embedded Voice Recognizer (Recognizes a few simple food words without setup.); Say food to cook (User says one word such as reheat, defrost, or popcorn.)
rationale: Natural speech replaces all knobs and buttons with no interface learning.
judge_comment: Voice control is intuitive, but it is already on the market, and noise and accents hurt reliability; it also doesn't clearly substitute something simpler or cheaper.

title: Food Scanner Auto-Cook
new_elements: Interior Food Scanner (Camera identifies food type and quantity.); Recognize and cook food (Sets time and power with zero user input.)
rationale: The microwave decides everything, so users only place food and close the door.
judge_comment: Zero-input cooking is ideal for the need, but camera recognition of food type, quantity and doneness is hard and costly.

title: No Turntable Mode Stirrer
new_elements: Mode Stirrer Fan (Rotating metal fan distributes microwaves without a turntable.); Even heating without plate alignment (Food can be placed anywhere and heats evenly.)
rationale: Removing the turntable eliminates the need to position or learn about the glass plate.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers are proven and cheap, and they remove placement concerns, but they only weakly relate to operation learning.

title: Transparent Casing No Lamp
new_elements: Transparent Microwave Shell (See-through body lets ambient light reveal the interior.); See inside without a lamp (No bulb or light switch is needed to check food.)
rationale: A transparent shell removes the lamp and any need to understand lighting controls.
judge_comment: A transparent shell is a radical substitution, but it does little for operation simplicity and creates microwave shielding and safety problems.

title: OLED Inner Wall Light
new_elements: OLED Interior Panel (Glowing wall panel replaces incandescent lamp.); Always-on soft illumination (Interior is visibly lit whenever the door opens.)
rationale: No separate lamp control exists, so checking food is automatic and simple.
judge_comment: An OLED wall panel is plausible and removes the lamp control, but it only slightly helps simplicity and would struggle with heat and microwave exposure.

title: Aroma Done Signal
new_elements: Aroma Release Vent (Releases a safe food scent when cooking finishes.); Smell-based done alert (User notices completion by smell instead of bell or display.)
rationale: A natural sensory cue replaces the mechanical bell and requires no learning.
judge_comment: A scent cue is novel and needs no learning, but it is unreliable, can be unpleasant, and does not simplify operation.

title: Sand Timer Cook Dial
new_elements: Sand Timer Dial (Visual hourglass replaces clockwork timer markings.); Watch sand to know time (User turns until desired sand amount remains.)
rationale: Time becomes a simple visual quantity rather than a numbered clockwork dial.
judge_comment: A sand timer is intuitive and visual, but it is imprecise and mechanically awkward for setting actual cook time.

title: Single Cook Knob
new_elements: Single Cook Knob (One knob replaces separate timer and power controls.); Turn to cook automatically (Any turn selects a safe default cook cycle.)
rationale: One control removes the power-level learning step entirely.
judge_comment: A single knob with a safe default cycle directly delivers no-learning-curve operation and is easy to build, though not very novel.

title: Weight Sensor Auto Power
new_elements: Plate Weight Sensor (Measures food weight when door closes.); Set power by weight (Microwave chooses power level automatically.)
rationale: Users never need to interpret the 5-step power knob.
judge_comment: Automatic power selection by weight removes a real confusing setting, though weight alone is a crude proxy for food type and time is still needed.

title: Foot-Pedal Door
new_elements: Foot Pedal Release (Pedal on floor opens the microwave door.); Open door by foot (No hands and no button-pressing technique required.)
rationale: A familiar pedal action replaces the small push-release button.
judge_comment: Opening the door by foot is plausible, but it only addresses the door and doesn't simplify the cooking controls that cause the learning curve.

title: Knock-to-Open Door
new_elements: Knock Sensor Latch (Detects a gentle knock on the door.); Tap door to open (Door pops open from a simple knock.)
rationale: Knocking is intuitive and removes the need to find a push button.
judge_comment: Knock-to-open is a novel interaction, but it risks accidental opening and does little for operating the cooking functions.

title: Gesture Control
new_elements: IR Gesture Sensor (Detects simple hand waves.); Wave to start (A wave starts a default cook cycle.)
rationale: No buttons or knobs need to be understood or touched.
judge_comment: Wave-to-start is very low learning curve, but a single default cycle is limited and accidental triggers are a safety concern.

title: QR Recipe Scan
new_elements: Door QR Scanner (Scans food package QR codes.); Cook from package code (Sets time and power from the QR code.)
rationale: The user scans instead of learning any timer or power settings.
judge_comment: Scanning package codes removes settings entirely for supported foods, but depends on packaging adoption and has an extra step of aiming the scanner.

title: Speech Three-Word Interface
new_elements: Three-Word Voice Chip (Only understands stop, start, and reheat.); Control with three words (Every operation uses one of three spoken commands.)
rationale: A tiny vocabulary makes operation obvious and nearly learning-free.
judge_comment: A three-word voice vocabulary is simple and plausible, but it needs the user to know the words and may misrecognize them in a noisy kitchen.

title: Moisture Sensor Stop
new_elements: Moisture Sensor (Detects steam inside the cavity.); Stop when food is hot (Cooking ends automatically at the right moisture level.)
rationale: Users do not need to set or understand time at all.
judge_comment: Steam-sensor auto-stop already exists in sensor-cook microwaves, but it removes time-setting entirely and fits the need well.

title: Icon-Only Presets
new_elements: Food Icon Buttons (Large pictures replace numbers and labels.); Press a food picture (One press cooks that food category.)
rationale: Pictures eliminate reading and make the correct action obvious.
judge_comment: Pictorial preset buttons are easy to build and understand, but they are very common and not radical.

title: Barcode Scanner Power
new_elements: Barcode Reader (Reads grocery barcodes inside the microwave.); Set power from barcode (No power knob interaction is needed.)
rationale: The microwave reads the package instead of asking the user to choose power.
judge_comment: A barcode reader inside the cavity is novel, but it is awkward and unreliable because packages often lack cooking data and the user must scan first.

title: Temperature Probe Cook
new_elements: Wireless Food Probe (Sticks into food and reports temperature.); Cook to temperature (Stops automatically at a safe internal temperature.)
rationale: Temperature replaces time and power settings as the only concept.
judge_comment: A wireless temperature probe makes temperature the single concept, but probe insertion adds a step and the idea is not new.

title: Antenna Rotation No Turntable
new_elements: Rotating Antenna (Antenna spins to distribute microwaves.); Even heating with no plate (Food can sit directly on the floor.)
rationale: Removing the turntable removes a whole setup step and its learning curve.
judge_comment: Stirrers and rotating antennas already exist in some ovens, and removing the turntable only slightly reduces operation effort, so it is a modest fit for the need.

title: Glow-in-Dark Interior
new_elements: Phosphorescent Liner (Interior walls glow softly after door opening.); See food without lamp (No lamp or window light is required.)
rationale: A passive glowing liner replaces the lamp and its operation.
judge_comment: A glowing liner is a quirky substitution, but the glow fades quickly and it does little for ease of operation.

title: Phone Notification Bell
new_elements: Bluetooth Beacon (Sends a done signal to nearby phone.); Phone tells you done (Bell is replaced by a phone notification.)
rationale: Users already understand phone alerts, so no new microwave signal is learned.
judge_comment: Phone alerts are familiar, but pairing a phone adds setup and works against a no-learning-curve goal.

title: Voice Announcement Bell
new_elements: Tiny Speaker (Speaks a simple done phrase.); Say food is ready (No bell pattern must be interpreted.)
rationale: Clear spoken words replace an ambiguous mechanical bell.
judge_comment: A spoken done message is simple, clear, and cheap, but talking appliances are not new.

title: Magnetic Auto-Close Door
new_elements: Magnetic Soft-Close Latch (Door closes and seals by itself when nudged.); Close without latching (No need to push until a click is heard.)
rationale: Self-closing removes the learned mechanical feel of the door latch.
judge_comment: A soft-close magnetic door removes the need to judge the latch click, but the safety interlock must still work and the gain is small.

title: Push-to-Open Door
new_elements: Push-to-Open Panel (Entire door front acts as a large release button.); Push anywhere to open (No small button must be located.)
rationale: A large target makes opening obvious and removes button-hunting.
judge_comment: Easy and feasible, but it only simplifies opening, not the core cooking operation, and push-to-open doors already exist.

title: Crank Timer Auto-Stop
new_elements: Spring Crank Timer (A simple crank winds a spring for cooking time.); Crank once to cook (Cranking any amount starts a safe auto cycle.)
rationale: A physical crank is intuitive and avoids numerical timer setting.
judge_comment: A wind-up spring timer is intuitive, cheap, and a real substitution for digital timing, though 'crank any amount' leaves cook duration ambiguous.

title: Default Two-Minute Cycle
new_elements: Always cook two minutes (Closing the door starts a fixed safe reheat cycle.); No Timer Control (Timer knob is removed entirely.)
rationale: A single default cycle means there is nothing to set or learn.
judge_comment: Zero learning curve, but a fixed two-minute cycle that starts on door close is inflexible and risky for unsuitable foods or empty cavity.

title: Auto Weight Defrost Button
new_elements: Defrost-Only Button (One button for all defrosting.); Defrost by weight (Weight sensor selects time and power.)
rationale: Defrosting no longer requires power-level or time knowledge.
judge_comment: A one-button defrost with weight sensing is clear and workable, but auto-defrost features are common and it covers only one task.

title: Steam Sensor Stop
new_elements: Steam Sensor (Detects steam release from food.); Stop at first steam (Cooking ends when steam is sensed.)
rationale: Automatic stopping removes the need to choose a duration.
judge_comment: Stopping automatically on steam removes duration setting entirely, though steam sensing is established and unreliable for foods that don't steam.

title: Camera Window Screen
new_elements: Door Camera Screen (Camera shows inside on an outer screen.); Check food on screen (No holes, lamp, or window are needed.)
rationale: A screen replaces the entire see-through window and lamp system with one familiar view.
judge_comment: A camera screen replaces the window and lamp, but it adds cost and the microwave-shielding problem, and it does little for operating simplicity.

title: LED Ring Light
new_elements: Door LED Ring (Ring of LEDs illuminates interior automatically.); Automatic interior light (No light switch or lamp replacement is considered by user.)
rationale: The light simply exists and requires no user action or learning.
judge_comment: Automatic interior lighting is already standard and only marginally helps operation, so it is not radical.

title: Hourglass Visual Timer
new_elements: Hourglass Display (Physical hourglass replaces numbered timer dial.); See remaining time (User watches sand fall instead of reading numbers.)
rationale: Time is understood visually without learning the clockwork timer scale.
judge_comment: A physical hourglass is intuitive and simple, but it is imprecise and mostly decorative, and it substitutes the display rather than the controls.

title: Sensor Cooking Only
new_elements: Multi-Sensor Array (Humidity, weight, and temperature sensors.); Cook without settings (All cooking programs are sensor-driven.)
rationale: Removing all manual controls makes the microwave as simple as closing the door.
judge_comment: Fully automatic sensor cooking directly removes the learning curve, though sensor reliability for diverse foods is a challenge and sensor cooking already exists.

title: Levitating Plate
new_elements: Magnetic Levitation Plate (Plate floats and rotates without a turntable motor.); Place food anywhere (No turntable alignment or removal is needed.)
rationale: A floating plate removes turntable handling and makes loading trivial.
judge_comment: A levitating plate is wild and removes turntable handling, but it is implausible inside a microwave cavity and only weakly tied to ease of operation.

title: Stirrer Spoon
new_elements: Microwave-Safe Stirrer (Simple passive stirrer sits in food.); Stir while heating (No turntable is needed for even heating.)
rationale: A familiar spoon replaces the turntable and its setup.
judge_comment: A passive stirrer is simple but does not address controls or the learning curve, and it can't truly replace a turntable.

title: Mood Buttons
new_elements: Mood Buttons (Buttons labeled Warm, Cook, Defrost.); Choose a mood (Each button starts a complete automated cycle.)
rationale: Everyday words replace technical power and time settings.
judge_comment: Plain-word preset buttons cut complexity and are easy to build, but they are close to existing preset buttons.

title: RFID Food Tags
new_elements: RFID Reader (Reads tags on microwave-safe containers.); Cook tagged food (Container tag tells microwave exactly what to do.)
rationale: Users never set anything because the container carries the cooking instructions.
judge_comment: Containers that carry their own instructions mean zero user input, but it needs a tagged-container ecosystem.

title: Smartphone Camera Aim
new_elements: Phone Vision Link (Phone camera identifies food through door window.); Point phone and cook (Phone sends a simple cook command.)
rationale: The familiar phone camera replaces all microwave controls for setting.
judge_comment: Phone-based recognition is feasible but adds app setup and phone handling, which works against zero learning.

title: One Big Start/Stop Knob
new_elements: Start/Stop Knob (One knob only starts or stops.); Press to start or stop (Internal sensors handle all cooking choices.)
rationale: A single start/stop control eliminates the entire settings panel.
judge_comment: A single start/stop control is the most direct fit for no learning curve, though sensor-only cooking is hard to make reliable.

title: Drawer Microwave No Door
new_elements: Drawer Mechanism (Sliding drawer replaces hinged door.); Slide open and closed (No door latch or push button is needed.)
rationale: A drawer is a familiar motion that removes door-handle learning.
judge_comment: A drawer is a familiar motion, but it does little for operating the controls and it is hard to engineer with microwave sealing, spills and safety.

title: Voice Reheat
new_elements: Reheat Voice Command (Only listens for the word reheat.); Say reheat once (Starts a safe automatic reheat cycle.)
rationale: One spoken word replaces all reheating controls.
judge_comment: A single-word voice trigger is simple and plausible, but it only covers reheating and voice control already exists on some models.

title: Single Popcorn Button
new_elements: Popcorn Button (Large dedicated button for popcorn.); Cook popcorn automatically (Listens for popping to stop.)
rationale: A dedicated one-press action removes all guesswork for a common task.
judge_comment: Popcorn buttons already exist on nearly every microwave, so this is highly feasible but barely novel.

title: Auto-Popcorn Listening
new_elements: Pop Sound Sensor (Microphone listens for popping rate.); Stop when popping slows (No timer setting is needed for popcorn.)
rationale: The microwave hears doneness, so the user only presses start.
judge_comment: Acoustic popcorn detection is a concrete mechanism that removes timer guesswork, though some microwaves already use similar sensing.

title: Plate Weight Presets
new_elements: Weight-Preset Plate (Plate detects food weight through contacts.); Cook by plate weight (Preset cycles are chosen automatically.)
rationale: Weight replaces manual setting and requires no user interpretation.
judge_comment: A weight-sensing plate that picks the preset automatically is a clever substitution for manual input, but contacts inside a microwave and the accuracy of weight alone are real challenges.

title: No Power Levels Auto
new_elements: One auto power mode (Power knob is removed and always auto-modulated.); Auto Power Modulator (Electronics vary duty cycle invisibly.)
rationale: The 5-step power knob disappears, so there is nothing to learn about power.
judge_comment: Removing the power knob simplifies things and is plausible, but time and start controls still remain, so the learning curve is only partly removed.

title: Color-Code Food Buttons
new_elements: Color-Coded Buttons (Red, green, yellow buttons match food types.); Press matching color (Color is the only instruction needed.)
rationale: Color matching avoids reading labels or learning settings.
judge_comment: Color-coded buttons are easy to build, but mapping colors to food types is arbitrary and not very radical.

title: Dial with Pictures Only
new_elements: Picture-Only Dial (Rotary dial has pictures instead of numbers.); Turn to a food picture (Each picture starts a complete cycle.)
rationale: Pictures remove all numeric timer and power interpretation.
judge_comment: A picture dial is intuitive and easy to make, though similar presets already exist and portion size is not handled.

title: Touch Anywhere Start
new_elements: Capacitive Door Touch (Door front senses touch anywhere.); Touch door to start (Any touch starts default cooking.)
rationale: There is no specific button to find, so operation is immediate.
judge_comment: Touching anywhere on the door to start is novel and simple, but the default cooking could be wrong and could start by accident, which is unsafe on an empty cavity.

title: Remove All Controls: Open Door Cooks
new_elements: Open door to cook (Closing the door starts an automatic sensor cook.); No Control Panel (All knobs, buttons, and displays are removed.)
rationale: With no controls at all, there is literally no interface learning curve.
judge_comment: Removing every control and cooking automatically on door close is radical and fully removes the learning curve, but sensor cooking accuracy and the lack of any override are real limits.

title: One-touch doneness sensor
new_elements: Doneness sensor (Infrared sensor detects food temperature.); Auto-stop when hot (Stops cooking automatically at target temperature.)
rationale: Removes timer and power decisions, making operation a single start action.
judge_comment: Strongly reduces decisions to a single start, but IR sensing of surface temperature inside a microwave is imprecise and the idea is not very novel; it also doesn't clearly substitute a part.

title: Voice-only start
new_elements: Voice command module (Microphone and speech recognition chip.); Hands-free operation (Starts and stops by spoken command.)
rationale: Eliminates all physical controls and learning by using natural speech.
judge_comment: Voice control is feasible and removes buttons, but users must still know what to say, and it is already common in appliances.

title: Barcode meal scan
new_elements: Barcode scanner (Reads packaged food barcodes.); Auto-setting from package (Sets time and power from product database.)
rationale: User only scans the package, so no manual settings are needed.
judge_comment: Scanning the package is simple and plausible, but it only works for packaged food with a database and doesn't cover everything else.

title: Transparent door film
new_elements: Transparent OLED film (See-through display replaces metal mesh and lamp.); See inside without light (Door itself shows interior clearly.)
rationale: Removes separate viewing light and door holes, simplifying the interface.
judge_comment: Visually interesting, but it barely relates to ease of operation, and a transparent OLED door must shield microwaves and withstand heat.

title: Touch-anywhere door
new_elements: Capacitive door skin (Entire door surface is a touch release.); Any-push open (Door opens when touched anywhere.)
rationale: No need to find a small button, reducing learning curve.
judge_comment: Opening the door is only a small part of the operation, and accidental touches would open it, though it does remove the need to find a button.

title: Smartphone one-button
new_elements: NFC tag (Passive tag read by phone.); Phone taps to cook (Phone sets cook cycle with one tap.)
rationale: Uses familiar phone interaction instead of microwave controls.
judge_comment: Phone tap is feasible but requires a phone and app setup, which adds a learning step rather than removing one.

title: Weight-sensing auto power
new_elements: Scale base (Weighs food on turntable.); Auto power by weight (Chooses power and time from weight.)
rationale: User places food and presses start, with no power or time decisions.
judge_comment: Place food and press start is very simple, though weight alone is a weak proxy for the right cook settings.

title: Steam-sensing stop
new_elements: Steam sensor (Detects moisture release from food.); Stop at steaming (Ends cycle when food is steaming.)
rationale: Removes need to know or set cooking time.
judge_comment: Humidity sensors already exist in sensor-cook microwaves, so it is practical and removes timing, but it is not very novel.

title: Thermal camera stop
new_elements: IR thermal camera (Maps surface temperature inside.); Stop at target temp (Ends cooking when set temperature reached.)
rationale: Automatic temperature target eliminates manual timing.
judge_comment: An IR camera is a concrete and plausible way to end cooking automatically, but the user still has to set a target temperature.

title: Smell-based doneness
new_elements: Electronic nose (Detects volatile aroma compounds.); Stop when aroma peaks (Ends cook at ideal aroma point.)
rationale: User does not need to estimate doneness or time.
judge_comment: An electronic nose is a radical way to remove all settings, but reliable aroma-based doneness detection is very hard.

title: Clap-on start
new_elements: Clap detector (Acoustic sensor recognizes clap.); Sound-triggered start (Starts cooking on a clap.)
rationale: One universal gesture replaces buttons and dials.
judge_comment: Clap start is simple and novel, but false triggers, unclear cook settings and food-in-the-oven safety limit its usefulness.

title: Foot pedal door
new_elements: Foot pedal latch (Floor pedal mechanically releases door.); Hands-free open (Door opens without hands.)
rationale: No need to locate or learn a door button.
judge_comment: Pedal door is mechanically easy but addresses only door opening, not the operation of cooking itself.

title: Single cook button
new_elements: One-button controller (One large start/cook button.); One-action cook (Starts a safe default cook cycle.)
rationale: A single physical action removes all setting choices.
judge_comment: One-button operation directly removes the learning curve and is easy to build, though it is an obvious idea and the default cycle may not suit all foods.

title: Auto power knob removal
new_elements: Impedance sensor (Measures load and reflected power.); Auto power level (Chooses optimal microwave power.)
rationale: Replaces the five-step power knob with automatic adjustment.
judge_comment: Automatic power selection by sensing load removes a control, but reliable impedance-based sensing of food is technically difficult.

title: Pictogram preset dial
new_elements: Icon dial (Dial shows only food pictures.); Picture-based selection (User points to food image.)
rationale: Recognition replaces reading or remembering power levels.
judge_comment: A picture dial is intuitive and cheap to make, but it is only a modest change from existing presets.

title: RFID food tag
new_elements: RFID reader (Reads tagged meal containers.); Auto recipe load (Loads cooking profile from tag.)
rationale: Food container carries all settings, so user does nothing.
judge_comment: Tag-based auto-programming eliminates the interface entirely, but requires packaged food ecosystem adoption and doesn't suit arbitrary foods.

title: Mechanical single-turn timer
new_elements: Single-turn spring timer (One 30-minute turn only.); One-motion timing (Twist once to cook.)
rationale: Replaces multi-turn clockwork with one simple gesture.
judge_comment: A single-twist mechanical timer is very simple and cheap, though such dial timers already exist and it offers limited control.

title: Voice announcer bell
new_elements: Voice announcer (Speaks 'done' instead of bell.); Spoken done alert (Clearly tells user cooking finished.)
rationale: Removes ambiguity of a mechanical bell.
judge_comment: A spoken 'done' is easy to build but only marginally helps operation simplicity and is a minor substitution.

title: Rotating antenna no turntable
new_elements: Mode stirrer (Rotating metal paddle distributes microwaves.); Even heating without turntable (No user turntable alignment needed.)
rationale: Removes the turntable and its placement learning.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers are already standard in many microwaves and only loosely address learning-curve simplicity.

title: Self-stirring bowl
new_elements: Magnetic stirrer bowl (Bowl stirs food automatically.); Auto stirring (No need to stop and stir manually.)
rationale: User does not need to learn stirring steps.
judge_comment: A magnetic stirring bowl removes a manual step, but a metal stirrer in a microwave is technically problematic and it's a niche accessory.

title: Gesture control
new_elements: Gesture sensor (Detects wave or swipe.); Wave to start (Starts or stops with a wave.)
rationale: A universal gesture replaces buttons and dials.
judge_comment: A wave to start is simple but doesn't set power or time, and it is a common, not very radical, idea.

title: Projected controls
new_elements: Projector (Projects only relevant buttons on counter.); Show only needed buttons (Interface adapts to food.)
rationale: Reduces visible controls to one or two choices.
judge_comment: Projected adaptive controls are novel, but the projector adds cost and complexity and it's unclear how the food is detected, so the idea isn't really a simplification.

title: Haptic knob
new_elements: Haptic dial (Dial gives physical feedback for one setting.); Guided single dial (Only one parameter is adjustable at a time.)
rationale: User cannot get lost because only one control is active.
judge_comment: A single haptic dial is simple and plausible, which fits the no-learning-curve need, though it is only moderately radical.

title: Auto door opening at end
new_elements: Spring latch (Releases door when timer ends.); Door pops open when done (No user action needed to open.)
rationale: Removes need to operate a door button after cooking.
judge_comment: A spring latch is cheap and feasible but only addresses the door at the end, not operating the microwave.

title: Color-changing window
new_elements: Thermochromic window (Window changes color with temperature.); Visual doneness (Shows hot/cold state without controls.)
rationale: User simply watches color instead of setting or reading displays.
judge_comment: A thermochromic window is a creative substitute for a display, but it shows temperature only and the microwave's cavity and food aren't a suitable thermal surface for it, so it doesn't help with operation.

title: Single reheat button
new_elements: Reheat button (One button for all reheating.); Default reheat (Uses sensors to reheat any food.)
rationale: Most common task becomes a single button press.
judge_comment: Highly relevant one-press operation, but similar buttons already exist and the sensor mechanism is vague.

title: Frozen/fresh toggle
new_elements: Two-state toggle (Only frozen or fresh choices.); Simple food state choice (Automatically sets time and power.)
rationale: Reduces power knob complexity to one binary choice.
judge_comment: Simple and easy to build, though a binary choice is too coarse to cover many foods and it is not radical.

title: Push-to-open no button
new_elements: Push latch (Push door to release, push to close.); Push door to open (No separate release button.)
rationale: The door itself is the only control, eliminating button hunting.
judge_comment: Push latch is cheap and intuitive, but it only addresses opening the door, not cooking operation.

title: Countdown voice
new_elements: Voice countdown (Speaks remaining minutes.); Spoken time remaining (No need to interpret dial markings.)
rationale: Users do not need to read or understand a timer dial.
judge_comment: Voice countdown is easy to build but does little to simplify setting up a cook, so it only loosely serves the need.

title: Auto defrost by weight
new_elements: Weight defrost (Weight sensor selects defrost cycle.); One-step defrost (Defrosts automatically by weight.)
rationale: Removes guesswork and power settings for defrosting.
judge_comment: Weight-based defrost removes guesswork and is plausible, but it is already common on existing microwaves.

title: QR recipe scan
new_elements: QR scanner (Reads QR code on food packaging.); Scan recipe (Loads exact cooking program.)
rationale: One scan replaces all manual time and power input.
judge_comment: Packaging QR scan removes manual input and is plausible, though it depends on codes being printed and similar products already exist.

title: Smart plate with sensor
new_elements: Sensor plate (Plate embedded with temperature sensor.); Detect doneness (Stops when food reaches serving temperature.)
rationale: User only places plate inside, no settings required.
judge_comment: A sensor plate that needs no settings is appealing, but embedding a sensor in a microwave-safe plate is hard because of the RF field, and wireless readout adds more difficulty.

title: No controls presence sensing
new_elements: Presence sensor (Detects food placed inside.); Start when food placed (Begins automatic cook cycle.)
rationale: The microwave behaves like an automatic appliance with zero controls.
judge_comment: Zero controls is very simple, but detecting presence without knowing the food or how long to cook risks overcooking or unsafe operation.

title: Magnetic auto-release
new_elements: Magnetic latch (Electromagnet releases door at end.); Auto door release (Door opens automatically when done.)
rationale: Removes the final manual step after cooking.
judge_comment: An electromagnet door release is easy to build, but it only removes the final step and does not address the learning curve for operation.

title: Big knob only
new_elements: Oversized knob (One large knob turns to cook.); Single control (Only one control exists on the appliance.)
rationale: No choices to learn because there is only one control.
judge_comment: A single big knob is simple and feasible but is essentially the old mechanical timer dial, so it is not radical.

title: AI camera doneness
new_elements: AI camera (Camera and neural net recognize food state.); Visual doneness recognition (Stops when food looks cooked.)
rationale: Automatic visual judgment replaces all user settings.
judge_comment: Camera-based doneness detection would remove all settings and directly serve zero-learning operation, though it is technically hard in a microwave and is not really a cheaper substitution.

title: NFC phone recipe
new_elements: NFC reader (Reads phone NFC tap.); Tap phone for cook (Phone sends cooking program.)
rationale: Uses a familiar phone tap instead of microwave dials.
judge_comment: Phone NFC tap is feasible and concrete, but it needs a phone and an app, which adds a learning step and is not very radical.

title: Touchless IR door
new_elements: IR proximity sensor (Detects hand near door.); Wave to open (Door opens with a wave.)
rationale: No button to find or learn for opening.
judge_comment: Wave-to-open is simple and intuitive, but it only covers opening the door, not the cooking operation.

title: Electroluminescent panel
new_elements: EL panel (Flat glowing panel lights interior.); Even interior light (No bulb to replace or switch.)
rationale: Lighting is automatic, removing any separate light control.
judge_comment: An EL panel for interior light barely touches operation simplicity, since lighting is already automatic in microwaves.

title: Transparent heating film
new_elements: Transparent heater (Conductive film heats and lets light through.); See through and heat (Combines door, window, and heater.)
rationale: Simplifies structure so user only sees food, not components.
judge_comment: A transparent heater film is radical and simplifies the structure, but it does little for ease of use and is doubtful as a microwave heating method.

title: One-button popcorn
new_elements: Popcorn button (Dedicated popcorn button.); Single-purpose quick cook (Perfect popcorn with one press.)
rationale: A common task becomes one press with no learning.
judge_comment: Popcorn buttons already exist on most microwaves, so this is helpful but not novel or radical.

title: Auto sensor reheat
new_elements: Humidity sensor (Detects moisture from reheating food.); Auto reheat (Reheats until food is steaming.)
rationale: User presses one reheat button and does nothing else.
judge_comment: Sensor reheat is a real, proven feature and very effective for zero-learning use, but it is already common.

title: Sound done alert
new_elements: Melody chip (Plays a distinctive melody.); Distinct done sound (Clearly signals completion.)
rationale: Removes confusion about whether the bell rang.
judge_comment: A distinct done sound only marginally helps operation simplicity and is trivial and not radical.

title: No timer auto off
new_elements: Thermal fuse (Physical cut-off at safe temperature.); Auto stop at temp (Stops without user-set timer.)
rationale: No timer to set or interpret; safety is automatic.
judge_comment: Replacing the timer with a thermal cutoff is bold, but a fuse is a one-time safety part and does not control food cooking well.

title: Simple app remote
new_elements: Bluetooth button (Single physical button pairs to app.); Remote one-tap (App shows one cook button.)
rationale: User uses one familiar app screen instead of microwave panel.
judge_comment: An app adds a pairing step and complexity, which contradicts no learning curve, though a one-tap UI is plausible.

title: Drawer microwave
new_elements: Drawer mechanism (Slide-out drawer replaces hinged door.); Push to open and close (One motion loads and starts.)
rationale: Removes door-button sequence and awkward loading.
judge_comment: A drawer with push-to-close auto-start simplifies loading, but safety and the unclear way it decides cook time and power limit the benefit.

title: Color-coded power
new_elements: Color dial (Power shown by color, not numbers.); Power by color (User chooses a color instead of watts.)
rationale: Color recognition is faster than learning power levels.
judge_comment: Easy to build, but colors still need a learned mapping to heat levels and don't address time, so the gain is modest.

title: Single lever
new_elements: Lever control (Push lever down to cook.); Push to cook (One lever motion starts cycle.)
rationale: Replaces multiple knobs with one lever.
judge_comment: A lever is a simple, intuitive input, but it's unclear how time or power is set, so it only works for one fixed cook.

title: Self-cleaning steam
new_elements: Steam capsule (Releases steam to clean interior.); Auto clean (Cleans itself without user settings.)
rationale: Removes cleaning mode learning and maintenance confusion.
judge_comment: It's a cleaning convenience rather than operating simplicity, and does little for the core cooking no-learning-curve need.

title: Universal AI cook button
new_elements: AI cook button (One button with sensors and learned presets.); One-button all foods (Detects food and cooks automatically.)
rationale: Every food task is reduced to a single universal button.
judge_comment: One-button automatic cooking fully removes the learning curve, but reliable food detection inside a microwave is technically hard, and the idea is quite generic.

title: Single Cook Button
new_elements: SingleCookButton (One physical button labelled only 'Cook'.); OneTouchAutoCook (Starts a safe default heating cycle with one press.)
rationale: Replaces multi-step power and time setting with one obvious action, removing learning curve.
judge_comment: Directly removes the learning curve, but one-button microwaves already exist and the default cycle is generic.

title: Weight Dial Auto
new_elements: WeightDialAuto (A single dial selects food weight, not power level.); AutoTimeFromWeight (Microwave computes time and power internally.)
rationale: Users think in food size, not watts or minutes, so operation becomes intuitive.
judge_comment: Weight-based input matches how users think, but it needs a weight estimate and still assumes food type.

title: Door-Close Auto Start
new_elements: DoorCloseAutoStart (Closing the door immediately starts a default safe cycle.); DoorCloseSensor (Simple switch detects door closure.)
rationale: No buttons must be understood; putting food in and closing the door is the whole interaction.
judge_comment: Zero-interaction start is very simple, but it risks accidental heating of empty or unsuitable items and may raise safety concerns.

title: Pull-to-Open Latch
new_elements: TugLatch (Door opens by pulling the handle directly, with no release button.); DirectPullOpen (Mechanical latch releases when the door is pulled.)
rationale: Eliminates the separate push-release button that new users often hunt for.
judge_comment: It removes a minor confusion point and is easy to build, but it does not address the core operation and it's not very radical.

title: Magnetic Reed Interlock
new_elements: MagneticReedInterlock (Magnet in door actuates a sealed reed switch.); MagneticDoorSafety (Cuts RF when the door is not closed.)
rationale: Replaces fussy mechanical lever interlocks with a hidden, foolproof alignment.
judge_comment: This is an internal safety component that users never notice, so it barely serves the no-learning-curve need, though it is concrete.

title: Single Safety Reed Switch
new_elements: SafetyReed (One safety-rated magnetic switch replaces three microswitches.); SimplifiedInterlockLogic (Still fails safe but with fewer moving parts.)
rationale: Less mechanism to misalign means the door simply works without user technique.
judge_comment: Reducing three interlock switches to one may weaken the fail-safe redundancy that safety standards require, and users would notice no difference in operation.

title: Optical Door Interlock
new_elements: OpticalInterlock (Light beam confirms door is closed.); BeamDoorSafety (Cuts power if beam is broken.)
rationale: No tactile latch force is needed; closing the door is enough.
judge_comment: An optical interlock is unlikely to meet safety standards as the sole safety mechanism, and it does little for ease of use.

title: Hall Effect Latch
new_elements: HallEffectLatch (Hall sensor detects door magnet silently.); ContactlessDoorSense (No mechanical switch wear or alignment.)
rationale: Door operation becomes silent and automatic, with no user-adjusted parts.
judge_comment: Hall sensors are feasible and robust, but the user-facing benefit is minimal.

title: Transparent No-Lamp Cavity
new_elements: TransparentCavity (Whole oven body and door are microwave-shielded transparent panels.); DaylightViewing (User sees inside without an internal lamp.)
rationale: Removes the lamp as a thing to notice or replace; seeing inside is effortless.
judge_comment: A fully transparent shielded body is radical but physically implausible, and it only loosely relates to simple operation.

title: LED Daylight Panel
new_elements: LEDPanel (Flat always-on low-power LED sheet lights the cavity.); EvenCavityLight (No bulb hotspot or replacement.)
rationale: A permanently installed light removes any user action around lighting.
judge_comment: An LED panel is plausible and low-effort, but it is an incremental change with little effect on learning curve.

title: Phosphorescent Cavity
new_elements: PhosphorescentLiner (Cavity liner glows softly after exposure to kitchen light.); GlowViewing (No powered lamp is needed to see food.)
rationale: A glow-in-the-dark interior requires no control or understanding.
judge_comment: Novel passive lighting substitute, but glow fades and does little to reduce operating learning, which is the actual need.

title: Electroluminescent Window
new_elements: ElectroluminescentWindow (Door glass itself emits light when powered.); SelfLitWindow (Illuminates cavity evenly with no separate bulb.)
rationale: The window simply lights up, so users never think about a lamp.
judge_comment: Electroluminescent glass is interesting, but it must be transparent and shielded from microwaves, and it barely touches operational simplicity.

title: Turntable-Free Stirrer
new_elements: ModeStirrer (Rotating metal stirrer blade distributes microwaves instead of moving food.); NoTurntableAlignment (Food can be placed anywhere on a flat floor.)
rationale: Eliminates the need to position or align a turntable correctly.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers are already used in many microwaves and remove turntable concerns, but this is not radical.

title: Fixed Turntable
new_elements: FixedGlassFloor (Non-rotating glass floor with hidden mode stirrer.); PlaceAnywhere (No moving user-visible turntable.)
rationale: A flat, fixed floor is simpler to use and clean than a rotating plate.
judge_comment: Flat-floor microwaves already exist; it simplifies placement and cleaning but is an obvious idea.

title: Rotating Antenna
new_elements: RotatingAntenna (Top-mounted rotating microwave antenna replaces turntable motor.); EvenHeatingNoSpin (Stirs microwaves without moving food.)
rationale: Users just put food in; there is no plate orientation or alignment.
judge_comment: Rotating antennas are in commercial products, so this is feasible and concrete but largely a duplicate of the stirrer idea.

title: Disposable Liner
new_elements: DisposableLiner (Paper or compostable tray sits on fixed floor and is thrown away.); NoCleanup (Food never touches the turntable.)
rationale: Removes cleaning and turntable handling from the user's mental model.
judge_comment: Reduces cleanup, but it does little for operating simplicity and the substitution is mostly a consumable tray.

title: Sand Timer Dial
new_elements: SandTimer (Visual gravity sand timer replaces mechanical clockwork.); VisibleCountdown (Time is shown by falling sand, not numbers.)
rationale: Anyone can see time remaining without learning timer markings.
judge_comment: A sand timer is intuitive and visible, but it is imprecise and awkward for varied cook times, and it doesn't remove the need to choose a duration.

title: Time-Only Knob
new_elements: TimeOnlyKnob (Single knob controls only minutes; power is fixed automatically.); OneDialOperation (No power-level decisions.)
rationale: Removes the confusing 5-step power knob, leaving one obvious control.
judge_comment: Removing power choices leaves one control and is easy to build, but it is a modest idea and limits cooking quality.

title: Default Two-Minute Start
new_elements: DefaultCook (Any start action runs a safe 2-minute cycle unless changed.); StartOnlyButton (One button starts the default cycle.)
rationale: A guaranteed default means users cannot fail to heat something adequately.
judge_comment: One-button default start is very simple, but a fixed 2 minutes can overcook or undercook and isn't truly adequate.

title: Steam Sensor Auto-Stop
new_elements: SteamSensor (Detects steam release and stops cooking automatically.); SteamDone (Ends cycle when food is hot throughout.)
rationale: Users do not need to know cooking times; the microwave senses doneness.
judge_comment: Sensor-based doneness removes the need to know times, which strongly serves no-learning-curve use, and the technology already exists in sensor-cook models.

title: Humidity Sensor Auto-Stop
new_elements: HumiditySensor (Cavity humidity rise triggers automatic shutoff.); HumidityDone (Infers when food has released enough moisture.)
rationale: No time entry is needed for common reheating tasks.
judge_comment: Humidity-based auto-stop already exists in sensor-cook models, so it is feasible and removes time entry, but it is not radical.

title: Weight Sensor Auto-Time
new_elements: WeightSensor (Floor sensor weighs food before cooking.); WeightAutoTime (Sets time and power from weight automatically.)
rationale: The microwave does the thinking; the user just places food inside.
judge_comment: Weight-based auto-time is plausible and removes decisions, but weight alone is a poor proxy for food type and heating need.

title: Barcode Auto-Cook
new_elements: BarcodeScanner (Scans packaged food barcode.); PackageAutoCook (Looks up and runs the package's cooking program.)
rationale: Users do not need to interpret package instructions or translate them to dials.
judge_comment: Barcode scanning removes the need to read package instructions, but it needs a database and adds cost, so it does not really substitute a cheaper part.

title: QR Auto-Cook
new_elements: QRScanner (Scans QR codes on food packaging or meal kits.); QRRecipeCook (Runs exact recipe cycle automatically.)
rationale: A simple scan replaces all manual time and power decisions.
judge_comment: QR scanning works like barcode scanning but depends on packaging adoption, so it is largely redundant with idea 3.

title: NFC Auto-Cook
new_elements: NFCReader (Reads NFC tag embedded in food container or sticker.); TapToCook (Tap container to microwave; cycle starts automatically.)
rationale: Physical tap is more obvious than dial programming for first-time users.
judge_comment: Tap-to-cook is intuitive and fairly novel, but it requires NFC tags on food containers, which limits it to a few foods.

title: Voice Cook Only
new_elements: VoiceCook (Only voice command accepted is 'cook'.); VoiceStartDefault (Starts default safe cycle.)
rationale: No interface learning beyond saying one word.
judge_comment: Single-word voice start is simple and feasible, but it is a modest idea, a default cycle may not suit every food, and it does little to substitute a part.

title: Motion Auto-Cook
new_elements: MotionSensor (Detects hand leaving the door area after closing.); HandsFreeStart (Starts cooking after door close and hand removal.)
rationale: No buttons or dials are touched at all for common reheating.
judge_comment: Hands-free start after the door closes is very simple, but it risks accidental starts and gives the user no control over time or power.

title: Proximity Auto-Cook
new_elements: ProximitySensor (Senses when a plate is placed inside.); PlatePresenceStart (Automatically begins a safe warming cycle.)
rationale: The act of placing food is the only operation required.
judge_comment: Starting automatically when a plate is placed is zero-learning, but detecting a plate and avoiding unsafe starts (empty or metal items) is tricky.

title: Thermal Camera Doneness
new_elements: ThermalCamera (Infrared camera reads surface temperature.); VisualDoneness (Stops when target temperature is reached.)
rationale: Users never estimate time; the oven knows when food is hot.
judge_comment: An IR thermal camera that stops at a target temperature removes the need to guess time, and it is plausible, though it reads surface temperature only and food varies.

title: Aroma Shutoff
new_elements: AromaSensor (Detects volatile aroma compounds released by hot food.); AromaDone (Stops cooking when aroma peaks.)
rationale: Doneness is sensed naturally, so no timing knowledge is needed.
judge_comment: Aroma-based doneness is wild and original, but reliable volatile-compound sensing in a microwave cavity is hard and varies by food.

title: Pop Sound Shutoff
new_elements: PopSensor (Microphone listens for popping rate.); PopDone (Stops popcorn when pops slow to a set interval.)
rationale: The user does not need to know popcorn timing or listen carefully.
judge_comment: Acoustic pop detection removes the need to know popcorn timing and exists in some microwaves, but it directly eliminates a common guess-and-fail step.

title: Phone Camera Window
new_elements: PhoneCamera (Uses phone camera placed against window to view inside.); RemoteViewing (No dedicated internal lamp needed.)
rationale: Users already know how to use a phone camera; no oven-specific viewing logic.
judge_comment: Using a phone camera against the window adds steps and does not simplify operation, and the window is mesh-shielded and awkward to film through.

title: Phone Notification Bell
new_elements: PhoneAlert (Microwave sends a phone notification instead of ringing.); SilentDoneAlert (Notifies user without a bell mechanism.)
rationale: Removes the need to understand or react to a mechanical bell.
judge_comment: A phone notification requires app pairing and connectivity, which adds a learning burden rather than removing one.

title: Light Flash Notifier
new_elements: FlashNotifier (Cavity light flashes instead of ringing a bell.); VisualDoneAlert (Signals completion without sound.)
rationale: Visual completion cue is universally understood and requires no learning.
judge_comment: A flashing light is simple and cheap and reads clearly, but it is an incremental idea and easy to miss if the user is not looking.

title: Auto Door Pop
new_elements: DoorPopper (Door gently pops open at end of cycle.); PhysicalDoneCue (Completion is shown by the door opening.)
rationale: Opening the door is an unmistakable, zero-learning completion signal.
judge_comment: A door that pops open at the end is an intuitive, unmistakable cue that needs no learning, though it adds a latch-release mechanism and has some safety and spill concerns.

title: Aroma Bell
new_elements: AromaBell (Releases a food-safe scent when cooking ends.); ScentDoneAlert (Alerts user by smell instead of sound.)
rationale: A familiar food smell signals completion without any controls or symbols.
judge_comment: Smell-based done alert is wild and removes symbols, but dispensing scent is impractical, may be unwanted, and doesn't address operation of controls.

title: Fixed Power Only
new_elements: FixedPower (Microwave always uses one safe power density.); FixedPowerSupply (No power-selection cam or knob.)
rationale: Removes power-level decisions that confuse first-time users.
judge_comment: Simple and cheap, but fixed power hurts cooking quality for defrosting and delicate foods, and it only partly addresses learning.

title: Pulse Button Only
new_elements: PulseButton (One button adds 10 seconds of full power per press.); AddTimePulse (Cooking time is built by visible button presses.)
rationale: Users can simply press until it feels right, with no numeric programming.
judge_comment: One button with additive time is nearly zero learning curve and very cheap, though not very radical.

title: Click Dial
new_elements: ClickDial (Dial clicks in fixed 30-second increments.); ClickCountTime (Time is set by counting clicks, not reading numbers.)
rationale: Tactile counting is faster to learn than interpreting a continuous timer scale.
judge_comment: A mechanical click dial is intuitive and feasible, but similar to existing dial microwaves.

title: Popcorn Button
new_elements: PopcornButton (Dedicated one-touch popcorn button with icon.); PopcornAutoCycle (Runs ideal popcorn cycle automatically.)
rationale: A single pictogram button handles a common task without any settings.
judge_comment: Popcorn buttons are already common, and it covers only a single task.

title: Pictogram Dial
new_elements: PictogramDial (Dial shows food pictures instead of power numbers.); FoodPictureSelection (Selects by food type, not wattage.)
rationale: Pictures are understood instantly across ages and languages.
judge_comment: Directly removes the learning curve with intuitive food pictures, though pictogram interfaces and presets already exist and are not radical.

title: Constant Full Power
new_elements: ConstantFullPower (No duty-cycle modulation; only on or off.); SimpleOnOffRelay (Replaces 5-step power cam with a relay.)
rationale: Eliminates the concept of power levels entirely for the user.
judge_comment: Removing power levels simplifies the interface, but it hurts cooking quality and the relay substitution is a modest change.

title: Thermal Fuse
new_elements: ThermalFuse (One-shot thermal fuse replaces resettable thermostat.); FixedOverheatProtection (Protects against overheating with no user reset.)
rationale: No reset or thermostat behavior for users to learn or manage.
judge_comment: Thermal fuses are standard already, and users never interact with this part, so it does little for ease of operation.

title: Software Thermal Model
new_elements: ThermalModel (Firmware estimates cavity temperature from power and time.); VirtualOverheatGuard (Cuts power before dangerous temperatures without a thermostat.)
rationale: Removes a physical component that users never need to understand.
judge_comment: A virtual thermal model is somewhat novel, but it is invisible to users and a software-only safeguard is risky.

title: Self-Bleeder Capacitor
new_elements: SelfBleederCap (HV capacitor with built-in bleeder resistor.); AutomaticHVDischarge (Discharges lethal voltage without service action.)
rationale: Safety happens invisibly, so ordinary users are not exposed to HV risk or procedures.
judge_comment: Bleeder resistors in HV capacitors are already common and the change has no bearing on user operation.

title: Solid-State Inverter
new_elements: SolidStateInverter (Semiconductor inverter replaces HV transformer, diode, and capacitor.); CompactRFGeneration (Generates magnetron drive with fewer HV parts.)
rationale: Fewer high-voltage parts means simpler, more reliable everyday operation.
judge_comment: Inverter microwaves already exist and the user-facing benefit for a no-learning-curve interface is indirect.

title: Solid-State RF Heater
new_elements: SolidStateRFHeater (Semiconductor RF source replaces magnetron and HV doubler.); InstantRFControl (Power can be controlled electronically with no warm-up.)
rationale: Electronic control hides all cooking complexity behind automatic algorithms.
judge_comment: Solid-state RF is a real emerging technology that enables automatic control, but the link to simple operation depends on an interface that isn't specified.

title: Conductive Gasket Choke
new_elements: ConductiveGasket (Soft conductive gasket replaces quarter-wave choke seal.); SimpleDoorSeal (Prevents leakage with a compliant seal.)
rationale: Door alignment becomes less critical, so users simply close it normally.
judge_comment: It's an internal seal change with almost no effect on the user's operation, and gaskets raise wear and leakage concerns.

title: Silicone Splatter Shield
new_elements: ReusableSiliconeSheet (Washable silicone waveguide cover replaces mica.); NoReplaceCover (User never needs to source or fit a mica sheet.)
rationale: A permanent easy-clean cover removes a maintenance task users would have to learn.
judge_comment: It's a plausible, easy swap that removes a minor maintenance task, but it doesn't make operation simpler and isn't radical.

title: Inductive Power Base
new_elements: InductiveBase (Microwave sits on a wireless power base instead of a cord.); NoPlugOperation (Place on base to power; no plug orientation or cord handling.)
rationale: Removes cord and plug fuss, making setup and daily use more automatic.
judge_comment: Wireless power for a high-draw appliance is inefficient and impractical, and it solves a non-problem since plugging in is already easy.

title: One-Touch Cook Button
new_elements: One-touch cook button (Single illuminated button starts a safe default cook cycle.); Starts default cook cycle (No time or power decision required from user.)
rationale: Replaces two knobs with one button, removing all setting decisions and learning.
judge_comment: Very simple and highly usable, but a one-button start already exists on many microwaves and is not radical.

title: Food-Icon Rotary Dial
new_elements: Food-icon rotary dial (Dial has pictures of common foods instead of numbers.); Selects automatic cook preset (One turn chooses time and power together.)
rationale: Icons replace numeric time/power settings, making operation guess-free.
judge_comment: Pictorial food presets remove numeric guesswork and are concrete, though preset accuracy for different foods and portions is a concern.

title: Touch-to-Open Door
new_elements: Capacitive touch release (Door opens with a light touch anywhere on the handle.); Touch-activated door opening (No push force or button hunting needed.)
rationale: Substitutes a mechanical push button with a touch surface, simplifying door access.
judge_comment: Capacitive door opening is a minor convenience that does little for the learning curve and risks accidental opening.

title: Magnetic Self-Latch Door
new_elements: Magnetic self-latch gasket (Door seals by magnet when pushed shut.); Self-sealing door closure (No latch button or lever to operate.)
rationale: Eliminates the separate door-release button and latch mechanics.
judge_comment: Removes a step of door operation, but microwave door safety interlocks and the need for a release complicate it, and the gain is small.

title: Voice Command Cooking
new_elements: Voice command module (Listens for simple commands like cook, reheat, stop.); Voice-set cooking cycle (User speaks a food name or action.)
rationale: Replaces physical timers and power knobs with natural spoken commands.
judge_comment: Voice control needs no learning in principle, but noise, accents and the need for a command vocabulary limit it, and it is not especially radical.

title: Default Start Only
new_elements: Start-only button (Runs a safe medium-power 2-minute cycle every time.); Fixed default heating (No settings, just start and stop.)
rationale: Removes all adjustable settings; one button is the entire interface.
judge_comment: Truly zero learning curve, but a fixed 2-minute cycle will overcook or undercook many foods, and it is a simplification more than a radical substitution.

title: NFC Recipe Tag
new_elements: NFC recipe reader (Reads a tag on food packaging and sets time/power.); Near-field communication (Short-range wireless tag reading.)
rationale: Cooking settings come from the package, so the user never learns the controls.
judge_comment: Package tags remove the need to learn controls, but this depends on food manufacturers adopting the tags, and NFC readers are cheap to add.

title: Barcode Scan Auto-Set
new_elements: Barcode scanner (Scans grocery barcode to infer power and time.); Optical barcode recognition (Low-cost camera plus database lookup.)
rationale: Power level is chosen automatically from the package, avoiding a confusing knob.
judge_comment: Scanning a barcode automates settings, but it needs a database and a scanner, and it is not simpler or cheaper than the controls it replaces.

title: Three-Icon Preset Dial
new_elements: Three-icon preset dial (Only reheat, defrost, and cook positions.); Preset duration selection (Each icon maps to a safe automatic time.)
rationale: Replaces numeric timer with three universally understood actions.
judge_comment: A three-icon dial is simple and easy to build, but similar preset dials already exist, so it is only mildly novel.

title: Weight Sensor Auto Power
new_elements: Weight sensor plate (Weighs food and selects power automatically.); Strain-gauge load cell (Cheap weight measurement under turntable.)
rationale: No power knob: the microwave figures out power from food weight.
judge_comment: A load cell is a plausible way to automate power, but weight alone doesn't indicate the food type or the time needed, so the user may still have to set things.

title: Add-30-Seconds Button
new_elements: Add-30-seconds button (Each press adds 30 seconds and starts immediately.); Cumulative simple timing (Duration is built by repeated presses.)
rationale: A single repeated button replaces a timer knob and its short-duration imprecision.
judge_comment: Highly intuitive and already common on real microwaves, so it is very relevant and feasible but not radical.

title: Doneness Dial
new_elements: Doneness dial (Positions marked less, normal, more.); Intuitive power adjustment (Maps directly to user expectation, not watts.)
rationale: Replaces abstract power levels with a familiar doneness choice.
judge_comment: Doneness mapping is easy to grasp, though it doesn't set time and the underlying logic is vague.

title: Foot Pedal Door Release
new_elements: Foot pedal release (Tap with foot to open door when hands are full.); Hands-free door opening (Mechanical or electric pedal linkage.)
rationale: Substitutes the small push button with a large foot target, easier to discover.
judge_comment: A hands-free door release is useful but only loosely tied to learning-free operation, and it adds a component rather than simplifying.

title: Push-to-Close Door
new_elements: Push-to-close magnetic latch (Door is simply pushed shut; no release button.); One-motion door closing (Door aligns and seals itself.)
rationale: Removes the separate release-button step from the door interaction.
judge_comment: It removes a step and is easy to build, but the door-opening method is left unspecified and a push-close latch is not new.

title: Transparent Shield Window
new_elements: Transparent shielding window (See-through conductive coating blocks microwaves without perforations.); Transparent conductive coating (Indium-tin-oxide-like film or fine metallic mesh.)
rationale: A clear window makes food status obvious without a lamp or hole pattern.
judge_comment: A transparent conductive window improves visibility but has little bearing on operation simplicity, and it is not cheaper than a perforated screen.

title: Metal Mesh Film Door
new_elements: Metal mesh film door (Adhesive transparent mesh replaces stamped perforated panel.); Printed fine-wire mesh (Sub-wavelength wire grid on polymer film.)
rationale: Cheaper, simpler window construction keeps visibility while reducing parts.
judge_comment: Cheaper window construction, but it does nothing for ease of operation, and the mesh film is already roughly how microwave screens work.

title: Auto-On Handle Light
new_elements: Handle-integrated auto LED (LED lights cavity when handle is touched.); Automatic interior illumination (No separate lamp switch or timer.)
rationale: Lamp behavior is automatic and tied to an obvious action, reducing learning.
judge_comment: Easy and intuitive, but it only automates the lamp, which is a minor part of the learning curve.

title: Humidity Auto-Off
new_elements: Humidity sensor (Detects steam release from food.); Automatic stop at doneness (Turns off when moisture peaks.)
rationale: No timer to set: the microwave senses when food is ready.
judge_comment: Removes the need to set a timer, which suits the need, though humidity sensing already exists in sensor-cook microwaves.

title: Temperature Probe Auto-Off
new_elements: Simple temperature probe (Single prong inserted into food.); Auto-stop at target temperature (Cooking ends when probe reaches preset.)
rationale: Replaces time counting with automatic temperature completion.
judge_comment: A temperature probe is well established and feasible, but inserting it and choosing a target temperature adds steps.

title: Steam Sensor Auto-Off
new_elements: Steam sensor (Detects boiling/steam burst.); Steam-triggered completion (Stops when steam indicates food is hot.)
rationale: User does not need to set time for reheating liquids or leftovers.
judge_comment: Automatic stop for reheating needs no timer, but it largely duplicates the humidity-sensor idea and is not radical.

title: Weight-Based Auto Cook
new_elements: Turntable weight scale (Measures food mass under turntable.); Weight-derived cooking time (Automatically chooses time from mass.)
rationale: Place food, press start; the scale replaces timer judgment.
judge_comment: Weight-derived automatic timing removes the main decision, though weight alone poorly predicts heating needs for different foods.

title: Power Toggle Preset
new_elements: Power toggle button (Cycles between gentle, normal, fast.); Simple power cycling (No rotary dial or numeric power levels.)
rationale: Replaces five-position power knob with an easy toggle.
judge_comment: Simple and feasible, but it only modestly simplifies and still leaves the time decision.

title: One-Button Doneness Cycle
new_elements: One-button doneness cycle (Press repeatedly to cycle cook, more, less.); Single-control combined time and power (Combines duration and power into one choice.)
rationale: Both timer and power are collapsed into one simple repeated choice.
judge_comment: A single-button cycle collapses controls, but it's ambiguous without a base time and may confuse users about what 'more' means.

title: Palm Sensor Door
new_elements: Palm proximity sensor (Detects hand near door edge and releases latch.); Proximity door opening (Door pops open without touching a button.)
rationale: Removes the need to find and press a small mechanical button.
judge_comment: Proximity-activated opening is feasible but addresses door opening, not the core cooking operation, and risks accidental opening.

title: Sliding Door Cavity
new_elements: Sliding microwave door (Door slides sideways instead of hinging and latching.); Slide-to-open access (Large vertical handle, no push button.)
rationale: A large sliding motion replaces hinge, latch, and button complexity.
judge_comment: A sliding door is intuitive but hard to seal against microwave leakage and has little effect on cooking operation.

title: Removable Magnetic Door
new_elements: Magnetic removable door (Door lifts off for cleaning and snaps back.); Detachable access (No hinges to align or latch.)
rationale: Removes hinge learning and awkward door swing.
judge_comment: A removable magnetic door barely addresses operation simplicity and creates safety and RF-shielding concerns.

title: E-Paper Countdown Dial
new_elements: E-paper countdown dial (Single dial; display shows only remaining time.); Bistable e-paper display (Low-power display that needs no backlight.)
rationale: Digital clarity with one physical control and no multi-button menus.
judge_comment: A single dial with a countdown-only display is intuitive and doable, though e-paper is a modest substitution.

title: Gesture Control
new_elements: Simple gesture sensor (Wave left for less, right for more, push for start.); Gesture-set cooking (No knobs or buttons required.)
rationale: Waving is universally understood and replaces all small controls.
judge_comment: Gesture control is novel, but it lacks discoverability and feedback, and it can misfire, so it is not clearly zero-learning.

title: Brown-Steam Knob
new_elements: Brown-steam knob (Only two food outcomes: brown or steam.); Outcome-based power setting (Maps directly to what user wants food to do.)
rationale: Replaces five abstract power steps with two understandable results.
judge_comment: Outcome-based brown or steam control is easy to grasp, but microwaves cannot brown without added hardware.

title: Single Food-Type Dial
new_elements: Single food-type dial (Rotary selector for meat, veg, liquid, frozen.); Combined food preset (One turn sets both time and power.)
rationale: A single familiar category choice replaces two separate controls.
judge_comment: A single food-type dial that sets both time and power is very easy to use and simple to build, though the idea is familiar.

title: Freshness Camera Auto-Timer
new_elements: Interior freshness camera (Small camera judges food color and steam.); Visual auto-stop (Stops when food looks done.)
rationale: Closed-loop sensing removes the need to estimate cooking time.
judge_comment: A camera that judges doneness removes the need to guess cooking time, but it is hard to make reliable and steam and splatter in the cavity complicate it.

title: Ice Sensor Defrost
new_elements: Ice-crystal sensor (Detects frozen state and thaw progress.); Automatic defrost cycle (No defrost time or power setting.)
rationale: The microwave handles defrost automatically instead of asking for settings.
judge_comment: Automatic defrost removes a confusing setting, though reliable ice sensing is difficult and similar sensor-based defrost already exists.

title: Popcorn-Only Button
new_elements: Popcorn-only button (Single button tuned for standard popcorn bags.); Popcorn preset (Fixed time and power for common snack.)
rationale: A highly visible single-purpose button avoids all timer/power confusion.
judge_comment: Popcorn buttons already exist on nearly every microwave, so this is trivially feasible but not radical.

title: Beverage-Only Button
new_elements: Beverage-only button (One button for reheating a mug of liquid.); Beverage preset (Safe automatic time and power.)
rationale: One clear button replaces two knobs for the most common task.
judge_comment: A beverage preset is common and simple, but it covers only a narrow task and is not radical.

title: Reheat-Only Button
new_elements: Reheat-only button (Single button for leftovers and plates.); Reheat preset (Auto time and power for a standard plate.)
rationale: Removes learning by offering a single obvious action for reheating.
judge_comment: A reheat button is common and easy to understand, but a fixed preset will suit plates of different sizes poorly.

title: Digital One-Knob Auto Return
new_elements: Digital one-knob timer (Knob sets time; display counts down; knob auto-returns.); Magnetic encoder with return spring (Simple digital knob replaces cam timer.)
rationale: Keeps the familiar one-knob interaction but improves precision for short times.
judge_comment: Practical and familiar, but an incremental tweak that adds little to the no-learning-curve goal beyond better precision.

title: Voice-Open Door
new_elements: Voice-open latch (Door pops open when user says open.); Voice-activated access (No physical door button.)
rationale: Door operation becomes another simple spoken command.
judge_comment: Voice opening is simple to use, but it needs a mic and a powered latch, and it is unreliable in noisy kitchens and not clearly better than a button.

title: Proximity Door Opening
new_elements: Body proximity sensor (Detects user standing in front of microwave.); Auto-open on approach (Door opens when user reaches toward it.)
rationale: Eliminates button pressing entirely during door access.
judge_comment: Auto-opening on approach removes a step, but accidental openings are likely and it is not a cheaper substitute.

title: Springless Latch
new_elements: Springless compliant latch (Flexing plastic latch replaces springs and levers.); Living-hinge compliance (Molded plastic flexures do the latching.)
rationale: Fewer mechanical parts make the door action more predictable and simpler.
judge_comment: A compliant latch is a genuine cheap, simple substitution, but it barely affects the user's learning curve.

title: Touchless Wave Door
new_elements: Wave-to-open sensor (Hand wave in front of door releases latch.); Touchless door release (No contact with microwave needed.)
rationale: A wave is easier to discover than a small push button, especially while carrying food.
judge_comment: Wave-to-open is intuitive and handy with full hands, but it is only moderately discoverable and adds sensor cost.

title: Manual Pump Timer
new_elements: Manual pump timer (Press a large dome to pump air and set time.); Pneumatic bellows timer (Air escape slowly counts down.)
rationale: A large squeeze/pump action replaces twisting a small timer knob.
judge_comment: A pneumatic pump timer is novel and mechanical, but pumping to set time is not obviously easier than a knob and has little precision.

title: Twist-and-Release Timer
new_elements: Twist-and-release timer (Twist once and release; spring returns to zero.); High-visibility detent timer (Large numbered ring with tactile stops.)
rationale: Keeps a single familiar motion but makes the timer easier to see and feel.
judge_comment: A big, tactile spring-return timer is simple and feasible but only a small step from existing mechanical dials.

title: Color-Coded Power Dial
new_elements: Color-coded power dial (Low is blue, medium green, high red.); Visual power selection (Color meanings replace numeric levels.)
rationale: Color coding communicates power state without reading or remembering steps.
judge_comment: Color-coded power levels are easy to understand and trivial to build, but they are incremental and ignore time setting.

title: Single Red Cook Button
new_elements: Single red cook button (Large red button starts and stops cooking.); Start-stop cooking (No other controls visible in normal use.)
rationale: A single red action button is self-evident even to first-time users.
judge_comment: A single start/stop button minimizes learning, but without a time or power input it implies a fixed cook duration, which limits usefulness.

title: Handle Weight Guess
new_elements: Handle weight sensor (Door handle measures tug from food weight.); Implicit weight-based time (Cooking time guessed when plate is placed.)
rationale: Removes timer setting by inferring portion size during loading.
judge_comment: Inferring weight from the door handle removes timer setting and is radical, but the sensing is unreliable and unlikely to give accurate cook times.

title: Smart Plate RFID
new_elements: Smart plate RFID reader (Reads embedded tag in compatible plate.); RFID plate tagging (Plate carries food type and cooking preset.)
rationale: The plate carries the instructions, so settings vanish from the user interface.
judge_comment: Plate-embedded RFID presets remove settings, but it requires proprietary plates and doesn't cover arbitrary dishes.

title: Thermal Camera Auto-Stop
new_elements: Thermal camera (Low-resolution heat map watches food surface.); Heat-map auto-stop (Stops when target temperature pattern appears.)
rationale: Food temperature is sensed directly, removing any timer input.
judge_comment: A thermal camera for auto-stop removes timer input and is plausible, since low-res IR sensors are cheap and already appear in some ovens.

title: Oven-Bag Sensor
new_elements: Oven-bag sensor (Reads printed sensor on microwave-safe bag.); Printed time-temperature indicator (Bag changes color or resistance as food cooks.)
rationale: Packaging tells the microwave when food is done, so users do nothing.
judge_comment: Packaging-based indicators are clever but need a new bag ecosystem and reliable sensing in a microwave field.

title: Automatic Power by Steam
new_elements: Steam-rate power regulator (Adjusts duty cycle based on steam production.); Closed-loop power control (No power knob needed.)
rationale: Power is controlled by food response, eliminating the power-level knob.
judge_comment: Steam-sensing closed-loop power is workable and removes the power knob, but it doesn't remove time or start decisions.

title: No-Settings Motion Dial
new_elements: No-settings motion dial (One large dial turns to any position to start a safe cycle.); Any-motion cooking (All positions run a preset; stopping is the only decision.)
rationale: Any turn works, so there is no wrong setting to learn.
judge_comment: A single any-position dial is very simple and easy to build, but it's a modest idea rather than a radical one and offers limited control.

title: One-Button Cook
new_elements: Single cook button with automatic time (Press once; internal preset times common foods and stops automatically.)
rationale: Removes duration dial decisions and countdown interpretation.
judge_comment: Presets for common foods exist already, and one press can't tell what food is inside, so it is not radical, though it clearly lowers the learning curve.

title: Thermal Auto-Shutoff
new_elements: Thermal probe auto-shutoff (Stops when food reaches target temperature, so no timer setting is needed.)
rationale: Eliminates timer guessing and overcooking anxiety for novice users.
judge_comment: A probe that sets cook end by temperature removes timer guessing, but it adds a probe the user must insert, and the idea is not new.

title: One-Button Full Power
new_elements: One-button full-power mode (Eliminates power-level choices; always uses optimal full power.)
rationale: Removes the confusing five-step power knob entirely.
judge_comment: Full power only is simple and cheap, but it hurts cooking results for many foods such as defrosting, and it is the opposite of radical.

title: Humidity Cook Stop
new_elements: Humidity-sensing cook stop (Detects steam and ends cycle without user time input.)
rationale: Turns cooking into a single start action followed by automatic stopping.
judge_comment: Steam or humidity sensors already ship in sensor-cook microwaves, and they do enable true start-and-walk-away use.

title: Hand-Wave Door
new_elements: IR proximity door release (Wave hand near door to unlatch; no button press.)
rationale: Removes small-button targeting for elderly or arthritic users.
judge_comment: Waving to open the door is a fresh touch that helps people with limited dexterity, but it addresses door opening only and could trigger by accident.

title: Auto-Open Door Pop
new_elements: Motorized door pop (Solenoid gently pushes door open after touch or timer end.)
rationale: Avoids pulling or pressing a latch and makes access obvious.
judge_comment: A solenoid door pop is feasible and mildly helpful for access, but it doesn't simplify cooking operation and isn't very radical.

title: Magnetic Push-to-Open Latch
new_elements: Magnetic push-to-open latch (Push door itself; magnetic catch releases, no separate button.)
rationale: Door operation becomes one intuitive push on the door itself.
