rationale: Green-yellow-red zones show short/medium/long at a glance.
judge_comment: Color zones make time choice intuitive, but they are imprecise and only a modest change from existing timers.

title: Auto-Stop Aroma Sensor
new_elements: AromaSensor (Detects food aroma in exhaust.); SmellDone (Stops when aroma indicates done.)
rationale: Stops when food aroma indicates done, no timer needed.
judge_comment: Removing the timer entirely is radical and ideal for zero learning, but reliable aroma sensing across foods is technically difficult.

title: Voice Announcement
new_elements: VoiceSpeaker (Speaks cooking status.); SpokenDone (Announces 'done' clearly.)
rationale: Speaks 'done' so user need not interpret bell.
judge_comment: Spoken status is clear but addresses only the end-of-cycle alert, not the operation itself, and it's common in appliances.

title: Musical Chime
new_elements: ChimeModule (Plays a short friendly chime.); FriendlyAlert (Distinct end-of-cycle sound.)
rationale: Familiar pleasant sound is easier to recognize than ding.
judge_comment: A friendlier chime barely affects ease of operation and is a trivial, unradical change.

title: LED Ring Progress
new_elements: LedRing (Circular LED around cavity shows progress.); ShowProgress (Ring drains to show remaining time.)
rationale: Ring drains to show remaining time, no reading.
judge_comment: A progress ring is easy to read but only aids understanding of time left; it doesn't simplify operation or substitute a part much.

title: Glow Cavity
new_elements: GlowLiner (Self-luminous cavity liner.)
rationale: Self-luminous liner shows food without bulb.
judge_comment: A self-luminous liner replaces the bulb, but that does little for ease of operation and is hard to make in a microwave cavity.

title: Single Start Button
new_elements: StartButton (One button starts a smart default cycle.); AutoCookAll (Uses sensors and defaults for any food.)
rationale: One button does everything with smart defaults.
judge_comment: One button with smart defaults gives a zero learning curve, though the idea is fairly obvious and reliable auto-cooking for any food is difficult.

title: Preset Meal Cards
new_elements: CardSlot (Slot accepts picture meal cards.); CardPreset (Card sets time and power.)
rationale: Insert a picture card for meal, no dials.
judge_comment: Picture cards replace the keypad with something simple and intuitive; they're easy to build but add the burden of managing cards.

title: Rotary Phone Dial
new_elements: RotaryDial (Old-style rotary dial for minutes.); DialMinutes (Dial each digit of minutes.)
rationale: Familiar rotary dial sets minutes by finger stops.
judge_comment: A rotary dial is a familiar, cheap substitute for a keypad, but entering digits is slower and not really simpler.

title: Pull-Cord Timer
new_elements: PullCord (Cord pull adds fixed time increments.); PullTime (Pull once for 30s, twice for 1min.)
rationale: Pull once for 30s, twice for 1min, intuitive.
judge_comment: A pull cord that adds fixed time increments replaces the keypad with an intuitive mechanical input, though precision and cord wear are concerns.

title: Foot Pedal Door
new_elements: FootPedal (Pedal opens the door hands-free.); FootOpen (Step on pedal to open.)
rationale: Hands-free opening with no button hunting.
judge_comment: A foot pedal makes opening easier but does not simplify the core operation of setting time and power, and the pedal adds complexity.

title: Motion-Sense Start
new_elements: MotionSensor (Detects a wave in front of the microwave.); WaveStart (Wave hand to start default reheat.)
rationale: Wave hand to start default reheat.
judge_comment: Wave-to-start with a default reheat removes all controls, but it risks accidental triggering and an empty or unsafe start.

title: Pop-Up Done Flag
new_elements: PopUpFlag (Small flag pops up when done.); VisualDone (Visible end-of-cycle indicator.)
rationale: Physical flag pops up when done, visible from afar.
judge_comment: A mechanical done flag substitutes for a beep but does little to simplify operation, so it only marginally serves the need.

title: Auto-Open Door
new_elements: MotorizedHinge (Hinge motor opens door at end.); AutoOpen (Door opens automatically.)
rationale: Door opens itself at end, no button.
judge_comment: An auto-opening door removes one step at the end of the cycle, but it is an add-on rather than a substitution that simplifies operation, and it adds cost.

title: Smart Leftover Preset
new_elements: LeftoverButton (Button for reheating leftovers.); LeftoverCook (Safe default for mixed meals.)
rationale: One button for common leftovers.
judge_comment: A one-button leftover mode is simple to use, but it is a standard preset, and mixed meals make a safe default vague.

title: Frozen Meal Preset
new_elements: FrozenButton (Button for frozen dinners.); FrozenCook (Safe default for frozen meals.)
rationale: One button for frozen dinners.
judge_comment: Frozen-meal buttons already exist on most microwaves, so this is easy to build but barely new and not radical.

title: Beverage Preset
new_elements: BeverageButton (Button for heating drinks.); BeverageHeat (Safe default for drinks.)
rationale: One button heats drinks safely.
judge_comment: Beverage buttons are already common and easy to use, with little innovation and no real substitution of parts.

title: Popcorn Preset
new_elements: PopcornButton (Button for popcorn.); PopcornCook (Optimized popcorn cycle.)
rationale: Dedicated popcorn button is universally understood.
judge_comment: The popcorn button is ubiquitous and understood by everyone, but it is the opposite of a wild idea.

title: Potato Preset
new_elements: PotatoButton (Button for baked potatoes.); PotatoCook (Optimized potato cycle.)
rationale: One-touch baked potato.
judge_comment: A potato preset is already standard and covers a narrow use case, so it adds little to the need.

title: Rice Preset
new_elements: RiceButton (Button for reheating rice.); RiceCook (Optimized rice cycle.)
rationale: One-touch rice reheating.
judge_comment: Rice presets are already common and are an addition, not a substitution, and they only cover one food.

title: Pictogram Door
new_elements: IconDoor (Door surface printed with simple steps.); GuideUse (Shows how to use microwave.)
rationale: Door surface shows simple steps.
judge_comment: Printed instructions replace a manual cheaply, but they add clutter and don't simplify the operation itself.

title: No-Knob Twist Timer
new_elements: TwistTimer (Twist ring like an egg timer.); TwistSet (Turn ring to set time.)
rationale: Twist ring like egg timer.
judge_comment: A twist ring in place of a keypad is intuitive and cheap, and old mechanical microwaves already used a dial, so it is only moderately novel.

title: Single Rotary Push
new_elements: RotaryPush (Turn to set time, push to start.); TurnPush (One control does both actions.)
rationale: Turn to time, push to start.
judge_comment: A single turn-and-push control replaces the keypad, is very intuitive, and is easy to build.

title: Magnetic Door Seal
new_elements: MagneticSeal (Magnetic closure instead of latch.); EasyClose (Door snaps shut easily.)
rationale: Door snaps shut without latch alignment.
judge_comment: A magnetic seal makes closing easier, but it is peripheral to operation and raises safety interlock and leakage concerns.

title: Self-Cleaning Mica
new_elements: SelfCleanCover (Mica cover with easy-clean surface.)
rationale: No need to remove/clean mica, less maintenance learning.
judge_comment: Easy-clean mica cover is a minor maintenance tweak and barely relates to learning-free operation, and it's not radical.

title: Arcing-Preventing Cavity
new_elements: ArcSafeCavity (Cavity with metal detector.); MetalDetector (Senses metal before power on.)
rationale: Detects metal and refuses to start, preventing scary mistakes.
judge_comment: Metal detection that blocks startup prevents a common user error, though reliable detection inside a cavity is tricky and it isn't a true substitution.

title: Superheat-Preventing Cup
new_elements: SafeCupSensor (Sensor in turntable detects liquid superheat risk.); StirAlert (Alerts user to stir.)
rationale: Alerts to stir drinks, avoiding dangerous surprises.
judge_comment: Alerting users to stir helps safety, but detecting superheat via a turntable sensor is technically doubtful and adds a step for the user.

title: One-Touch Keep Warm
new_elements: WarmButton (Button keeps food warm.); KeepWarm (Gentle default warming cycle.)
rationale: Single button keeps food warm.
judge_comment: A single keep-warm button is simple and easy to build, but it is incremental and thinly described.

title: Automatic Popcorn Stop
new_elements: PopSensor (Microphone listens for popcorn pops.); AutoPopStop (Stops when pops slow.)
rationale: Listens for pops and stops, no guessing.
judge_comment: Acoustic popcorn detection removes guesswork and is feasible (some products already exist), with a clear mechanism.

title: Child-Proof Single Action
new_elements: ChildSafeButton (Long-press button opens door.); LongPress (Single long press is simple but safe.)
rationale: One long press opens, simple but safe.
judge_comment: A long-press door button is easy to build but barely addresses ease of operation and may add friction.

title: No-Display Minimalism
new_elements: BlankPanel (Blank panel hiding all but three buttons.); HiddenControls (Only essential controls exposed.)
rationale: Only three buttons visible; no clock to set.
judge_comment: A three-button panel with no clock is simple and effective, though it is a known minimalism approach.

title: Auto Clock Off
new_elements: NoClockPanel (Control panel without clock.)
rationale: Removes clock setting chore that confuses users.
judge_comment: Removing the clock eliminates a real setup chore, but it is a small and obvious change.

title: Universal Icons
new_elements: UniversalIconSet (Icons for reheat, defrost, beverage, popcorn.); CrossLanguage (No words needed to understand.)
rationale: Icons understood across languages and ages.
judge_comment: Language-independent icons for common tasks lower the learning curve, though many microwaves already use them.

title: Default Cook Mode
new_elements: DefaultCook (Closing door starts safe default cook.); ZeroSetup (No settings required.)
rationale: Closing door starts a safe default cook with no setup.
judge_comment: Starting a safe default cook when the door closes removes all setup, but it risks accidental or unsafe heating and needs load sensing.

title: One-Touch Cook Dial
new_elements: One-Touch Cook Dial (A single rotary dial with push-to-start and preset detents for common foods.); Set time and power in one gesture (Collapses duration and power choices into one intuitive action.)
rationale: Replaces two separate knobs with one obvious dial so users need no learning curve.
judge_comment: Easy to use and very feasible, but it is a familiar dial with presets, so it is not radical.

title: Voice Cook
new_elements: Always-listening voice intent parser (Recognizes simple phrases like 'reheat soup' and sets time/power automatically.); Cook by spoken intent (Lets the user start cooking without touching or reading controls.)
rationale: Natural speech removes the need to learn knob positions or power levels.
judge_comment: Voice control removes the need to learn controls, but it already exists in some models and is vulnerable to noise and misrecognition.

title: See-and-Cook Camera
new_elements: Interior food-recognition camera (A tiny camera recognizes common foods and suggests a one-touch cook cycle.); Auto-select cook program (Chooses time and power from visual food type.)
rationale: The microwave decides the settings, so the user only presses one button.
judge_comment: A camera that recognizes food and picks the program is a bold step toward zero learning, though recognition accuracy and cost are concerns.

title: Doneness Sensor Auto-Stop
new_elements: IR thermopile doneness sensing (Non-contact infrared reads surface temperature and stops when food is hot.); Detect doneness and stop (Ends cooking automatically instead of relying on a timer.)
rationale: Users no longer need to guess time or power for reheating.
judge_comment: Auto-stop on IR temperature removes time and power guesswork, but surface-only readings and container effects limit accuracy.

title: Pictogram Food Dial
new_elements: Pictogram food dial (A dial with food icons instead of power numbers or text.); Select food type (Maps an intuitive picture to an automatic power profile.)
rationale: Pictures eliminate reading and memorizing power-level numbers.
judge_comment: Icons are intuitive and cheap to build, but food-preset dials are a fairly obvious and incremental idea.

title: Fixed Minute Buttons
new_elements: Three fixed-time buttons (Large 1, 2, and 3 minute buttons with tactile feedback.); One-touch duration (Starts a common cook time with a single press.)
rationale: Fixed buttons remove fine timer adjustment and are easy for all users.
judge_comment: Directly removes timer adjustment and is simple to use, but similar preset buttons already exist and it is not radical.

title: Gesture Door
new_elements: IR gesture door latch (A wave of the hand releases the door without a button.); Hands-free door open (Opens the door using a simple gesture.)
rationale: No button to find or press makes door operation self-evident.
judge_comment: A hands-free door is novel, but gesture detection can misfire and it addresses only door opening, not the main operation.

title: Magnetic Hall Interlock
new_elements: Magnetic Hall-effect interlock (A magnet in the door and a Hall sensor replace mechanical microswitches.); Detect door closed (Senses door position without moving switch arms.)
rationale: A simpler, more reliable closed-door check avoids fiddly latch learning.
judge_comment: A technically sound part swap, but invisible to the user and does little for the no-learning-curve need.

title: Voice Done Announcement
new_elements: Voice announcer (A small speaker says 'done' instead of or in addition to a ding.); Spoken end alert (Announces completion in plain language.)
rationale: Users immediately understand the end signal without interpreting a bell.
judge_comment: Easy to build and mildly clearer, but it only affects the end alert, not operation.

title: Pull-Cord Timer
new_elements: Pull-cord kitchen timer (A familiar pull-cord mechanism starts a fixed short cook.); Pull to start (Starts cooking with one intuitive tug.)
rationale: The gesture is already familiar from kitchen timers, so no instruction is needed.
judge_comment: A familiar pull-cord start is intuitive and quirky, but a mechanical cord on a microwave is awkward and offers a fixed time only.

title: Full-Power Only Simplicity
new_elements: Always full power (Removes power-level choice entirely for reheating and boiling.); No low-power defrost mode (Limits some functions but greatly simplifies use.)
rationale: Removing the power knob removes a decision point for novice users.
judge_comment: Removing power levels does simplify use and is easy to build, but it is a feature removal rather than a radical substitution and it hurts results such as defrosting.

title: Weight-Sensing Turntable Auto Power
new_elements: Weight-sensing turntable (The turntable support measures food weight.); Auto duty cycle (Sets power cycling from weight without user input.)
rationale: The user just places food and presses start; power level is chosen automatically.
judge_comment: A weight-sensing turntable that sets power automatically is plausible and cuts the decisions, though weight alone is a crude proxy for the right settings.

title: Transparent See-Inside Door
new_elements: Transparent IR-blocking window (A clear microwave-safe panel lets users see inside without an internal lamp.); See inside without lamp (Provides visual feedback passively.)
rationale: No lamp or lamp replacement makes the experience simpler and more reliable.
judge_comment: A lamp-free see-through door only loosely serves the no-learning-curve need, and without a lamp or a mesh the door would be hard to see through or to shield.

title: Metamaterial Transparent Shield
new_elements: Metamaterial microwave-transparent shield (A frequency-selective surface blocks microwaves while being fully clear.); See-through RF containment (Contains radiation without perforated mesh or a lamp.)
rationale: A clear, hole-free door removes visual clutter and the need to understand mesh windows.
judge_comment: A transparent metamaterial RF shield is a bold idea, but it is largely cosmetic for simplicity of operation and is hard to make at consumer cost.

title: Weight Plus One Cook Button
new_elements: Weight sensor with one Cook button (Weighs food, then a single button starts a suitable cycle.); Automatic time and power (Infers settings from weight with no dials.)
rationale: One button is the ultimate no-learning interface for reheating.
judge_comment: A single Cook button with weight-based automatic settings is the most direct answer to a zero-learning interface and is feasible, though it is not very novel.

title: Single Click Dial
new_elements: One dial, click to start (A single dial selects preset and starts with a click.); All control via dial press (Combines selection and confirmation.)
rationale: One physical control with a click is familiar from car stereos and smart thermostats.
judge_comment: Simple and feasible single-control design, but the idea is incremental, and the dial's cheaper-substitute role is only loosely defined.

title: Magnetic Pull Door
new_elements: Magnetic pull-open door (A soft magnetic catch holds the door shut; the user simply pulls it open.); Open by pulling (Eliminates the release button.)
rationale: Pulling a door is universally understood, unlike finding a push-release button.
judge_comment: A magnetic pull door replaces the release button cheaply and intuitively, but it only addresses opening and is not radical.

title: Doneness Dial
new_elements: Doneness dial (A dial labeled warm, hot, and piping hot rather than power levels.); Set desired final temperature (Maps an intuitive outcome to automatic power.)
rationale: Users choose an outcome, not an engineering parameter.
judge_comment: Outcome-based doneness selection removes the need to know power levels or times, though reliable automatic temperature sensing is harder to build.

title: Icon-Only Panel
new_elements: Icon-only operation (All controls use universal symbols with no text labels.); Universal symbol fascia (Large contrasting icons replace words and numbers.)
rationale: Icons are understood across languages and require no manual reading.
judge_comment: Icon-only panels are already common, so the idea is easy to build but not novel, and it gives few details.

title: Voice Timer
new_elements: Voice timer assistant (User says a time and the microwave counts down and stops.); Set timer by voice (Removes timer knob manipulation.)
rationale: Speaking a duration is simpler than learning timer scale and direction.
judge_comment: Voice input is easy to use with no learning curve, but it is already available on existing products and adds cost rather than simplifying.

title: Foot Pedal Door
new_elements: Foot pedal door release (A floor-level pedal opens the door hands-free.); Open door with foot (Useful when hands are full.)
rationale: A pedal is an obvious physical action that needs no hand-eye instruction.
judge_comment: Hands-free door opening is convenient but barely affects the operational learning curve, and it adds a mechanical linkage rather than substituting a part for simplicity.

title: Mode Stirrer No Turntable
new_elements: Mode stirrer (A rotating metal paddle distributes microwaves without moving the food.); Even heating without turntable (No tray alignment, removal, or cleaning of roller ring.)
rationale: Users simply place food anywhere, with no turntable parts to understand.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers already exist in many microwaves, so it is a real substitution that removes turntable fiddling, but it is not radical and does not simplify the controls.

title: Self-Centering Turntable
new_elements: Self-centering turntable (A funnel-like support centers any dish automatically.); Drop-in turntable placement (No need to align coupler or roller ring.)
rationale: Removes the fiddly step of seating the tray correctly.
judge_comment: A self-centering support removes a minor setup step and is plausible, though the mechanism is vague and may hinder dish rotation.

title: Temperature Target Dial
new_elements: Temperature target dial (Dial sets a final food temperature rather than a power level.); Set final temperature (Cooking stops when the target is reached.)
rationale: The user thinks in terms of hot food, not power percentages.
judge_comment: Setting a target temperature is intuitive, but reliably sensing food core temperature inside a microwave is hard and probes add complexity.

title: NFC Recipe Tap
new_elements: NFC recipe tag reader (Tapping a food package or recipe card sets time and power automatically.); Tap to cook (No manual settings for tagged foods.)
rationale: A tap is a familiar smartphone-like gesture that hides all cooking parameters.
judge_comment: Tap-to-cook is very simple for users and technically feasible, but it depends on tagged packaging and does not help untagged foods.

title: Crank Timer with Sensor Stop
new_elements: Crank timer with auto-stop (One crank sets a generous time; doneness sensor stops early if needed.); Crank and forget (No precision needed from the timer.)
rationale: Over-setting time is safe because the sensor ends cooking.
judge_comment: A crank timer paired with a doneness sensor is simple and forgiving, though reliable sensing of doneness across foods is hard.

title: Three Recipe Buttons
new_elements: Three recipe buttons (Reheat, defrost, and melt buttons with fixed logic.); Preset modes (Covers common tasks with no power setting.)
rationale: Users choose a task name rather than decode power cycling.
judge_comment: Preset buttons are already common on microwaves and are easy to build, but they are barely a radical idea.

title: Minute Plus Button
new_elements: Minute-plus button (Each press adds 30 seconds and starts immediately.); Add time by pressing (No dial setting before cooking.)
rationale: A single repeated button is the simplest possible timer interaction.
judge_comment: A press-to-add-30-seconds button is already widely available and is very easy to use, but it is not radical.

title: Drawer Microwave
new_elements: Drawer-style microwave (Food is placed in a pull-out drawer instead of through a hinged door.); Slide drawer access (Eliminates door button and swing clearance.)
rationale: Sliding a drawer open is intuitive and avoids door-latch learning.
judge_comment: Drawer microwaves exist but are expensive, and they do little to reduce the learning needed for operation.

title: Top-Loading Microwave
new_elements: Top lid with hinge (A lift-up lid replaces the front door.); Open by lifting (Allows drop-in access like a pot.)
rationale: Lifting a lid is a primitive kitchen action requiring no instruction.
judge_comment: A top-loading lid is intuitive and different, but it has ergonomic and spill issues and does not simplify the controls.

title: Pull Handle Door
new_elements: Full-width pull handle (The door is opened by pulling a prominent handle.); Open door directly (No separate release button.)
rationale: A handle affords pulling without any learned button behavior.
judge_comment: Intuitive and feasible, but pull handles already exist on many microwaves and it does not address operation of the cooking controls.

title: Capacitive Gesture Strip
new_elements: Capacitive gesture strip (Swipe or tap once to reheat, twice to defrost.); One-tap cook (Simple touch gestures replace knobs.)
rationale: Touch gestures are familiar from phones and require no mechanical learning.
judge_comment: Touch gestures are plausible, but tap-count mappings like once for reheat and twice for defrost must be learned, and touch panels are already common.

title: Wind-Up Timer Auto-Off
new_elements: Wind-up timer with auto-off (A simple wind-up timer runs the microwave only while unwinding.); Set and forget (No digital settings or precision.)
rationale: The mechanism itself communicates that turning it starts cooking.
judge_comment: A mechanical wind-up dial is a true substitution that is instantly understood and cheap, and it was once common, but it is imprecise and a good fit for a no-learning-curve goal.

title: Load-Sensing Power Control
new_elements: Load-sensing magnetron power control (Detects food load and adjusts duty cycle automatically.); Auto power (No manual power level selection.)
rationale: Power is handled invisibly, so the user only chooses time or food type.
judge_comment: Auto power removes a decision, but load sensing is hard to do reliably and it is invisible to the user, so it only partly helps the interface.

title: Countdown Light Ring
new_elements: Countdown light ring (A colored ring counts down and flashes when done.); Visual end signal (Shows progress and completion without sound.)
rationale: A single glanceable indicator removes ambiguity about when food is ready.
judge_comment: A glanceable light ring is easy to build and clear, but it only handles feedback, not input, and is a modest idea.

title: Self-Aligning RF Gasket
new_elements: Self-aligning magnetic RF gasket (A flexible magnetic seal snaps the door into RF-safe alignment.); Seal without precise closing (The door does not need careful positioning.)
rationale: Users can close the door casually and still be safe.
judge_comment: A magnetic gasket is a plausible substitution, but RF leakage safety is hard to guarantee and closing the door is not the main learning-curve barrier.

title: Pneumatic Auto-Open Hinge
new_elements: Pneumatic auto-open hinge (Pressing anywhere on the door gently powers it open.); Door opens itself (No latch release or pulling.)
rationale: A soft push anywhere is more discoverable than a dedicated release button.
judge_comment: A self-opening door is a simple, discoverable interaction, but it addresses only a minor part of operation and adds safety and mechanical complexity.

title: Barcode Scanner Cook
new_elements: Barcode/UPC scanner (Scans packaged food barcodes and sets a cook cycle.); Auto-set cook cycle (Eliminates manual time and power entry.)
rationale: Scanning is a familiar store-checkout action that hides all settings.
judge_comment: Barcode scanning removes manual settings using a familiar action and is feasible, though it works only for packaged foods with a database.

title: RFID Food Tag
new_elements: RFID food tag reader (Reads a tag on the packaging to identify the food and settings.); Identify and cook tagged food (No user programming required.)
rationale: The appliance recognizes the food, so the user does nothing but close the door.
judge_comment: RFID-tagged packaging gives zero-input cooking, but it depends on food makers adopting tags and on metal-in-cavity concerns.

title: Interior Camera AI Doneness
new_elements: Interior camera with AI doneness model (Watches color, steam, and bubbling to stop at the right time.); Vision-based doneness (Automatically terminates cooking.)
rationale: The microwave watches the food, removing the need for user timing skill.
judge_comment: A camera that judges doneness removes all timing decisions and works for any food, though it is costly and hard to make reliable in steam.

title: Big Cook and Cancel Buttons
new_elements: Big Cook and Cancel buttons (Two large physical buttons cover all normal use.); One-button operation (Cook starts automatically; Cancel stops.)
rationale: Two obvious buttons eliminate interface decisions.
judge_comment: Very simple and effective for zero learning curve, but not radical and similar to existing minimalist microwaves.

title: Proximity Auto-Open
new_elements: Proximity sensor door (Door opens automatically when a hand approaches.); Approach to open (No button or gesture training.)
rationale: The door responds to natural approach behavior.
judge_comment: Auto-opening door is novel but addresses only door opening, and can be unintended or unsafe; it doesn't cover cooking operation.

title: Single Reheat Button
new_elements: Single Reheat button (One large button for the most common task.); Instant reheat (Uses a default safe cycle.)
rationale: A dedicated reheat button matches the dominant use case with zero setup.
judge_comment: Single reheat button is easy to use and feasible but covers only one use case and is common.

title: Color-Coded Food Buttons
new_elements: Color-coded food buttons (Beverage, plate, frozen, and popcorn buttons in distinct colors.); Visual food task selection (Buttons map to common foods without numbers.)
rationale: Color and food names make selection immediate and memorable.
judge_comment: Color-coded food buttons are intuitive and concrete, though multiple categories add some choice and are an incremental idea.

title: One-Touch Popcorn Key
new_elements: One-touch popcorn key (A dedicated popcorn button with optimal timing.); Cook popcorn automatically (No settings needed for a common snack.)
rationale: A single labeled key removes all guesswork for a frequent use.
judge_comment: Popcorn buttons already exist on most microwaves, so it is feasible but unoriginal and narrow.

title: Mechanical Detent Timer
new_elements: Mechanical detent timer (Timer only stops at 1, 3, 5, and 10 minute detents.); Choose simple duration (Prevents imprecise short-time confusion.)
rationale: Detents guide the hand to valid choices without reading.
judge_comment: Detent timer simplifies choices and is easy to build, but mechanical timers are old and not radical.

title: Moisture-Sensor Auto Power
new_elements: Humidity/moisture sensor auto-power (Senses steam and adjusts power automatically.); Auto power by moisture (No power knob needed.)
rationale: The microwave senses cooking progress and hides power control.
judge_comment: Sensor cooking exists in many microwaves, but removing the power control does reduce what the user must learn.

title: Clear Window No Lamp
new_elements: Clear window with external room light (Uses ambient kitchen light instead of an internal bulb.); Passive visibility (No lamp to burn out or replace.)
rationale: No lamp maintenance or switch logic keeps the product simpler.
judge_comment: Dropping the lamp saves cost but makes the food harder to see and does little for ease of operation.

title: Gravity Latch Door
new_elements: Gravity latch door (Door closes by its own weight and seals; opening is a light pull.); Automatic door sealing (No complex latch alignment.)
rationale: The door works by gravity and a pull, avoiding latch-button learning.
judge_comment: A self-closing door is intuitive, but a safety interlock is still needed and gravity sealing is questionable.

title: Universal Symbols Plus Braille
new_elements: Tactile universal control surface (Icons with Braille and raised shapes on every control.); No-look operation (Users can identify controls by touch.)
rationale: Tactile icons let anyone operate without reading or visual learning.
judge_comment: Tactile controls help accessibility and are easy to make, but they add labelling without simplifying operation or substituting any part.

title: One-Button Cook
new_elements: Single auto-cook button (One large button starts an automatic cook cycle.); Infers time and power automatically (Sensors choose duration and duty cycle.)
rationale: Removes the need to understand time and power knobs, directly serving.
judge_comment: Directly serves zero-learning operation, but sensor inference is vague and one-button auto-cook exists already.

title: Weight-Sensing Auto Heat
new_elements: Cavity weight sensor (Measures food mass on the tray.); Auto-selects power from mass (Maps weight to an automatic power level.)
rationale: Eliminates power-level decisions, making operation a simple place-and-go action for.
judge_comment: Weight sensing is plausible and removes power choice, but mass alone poorly determines cook time and it's not radical.

title: RFID Meal Tag
new_elements: RFID/NFC cook-code reader (Reads embedded cooking instructions from packaging.); Tagged meal packaging (Meal pack carries time and power code.)
rationale: Turns cooking into a scan-and-start action, requiring no user learning for.
judge_comment: Scan-and-start is simple for tagged meals, though it depends on packaging ecosystem and fails for untagged food.

title: Barcode Scan & Go
new_elements: Barcode scanner (Reads meal barcode for cook settings.); Auto-sets cook program (Looks up time and power from code.)
rationale: Replaces manual knob setting with a familiar scan gesture, reducing learning curve for.
judge_comment: Barcode lookup is easily built and concrete, but needs a database and the scan step adds a bit of friction; existing products do similar.

title: Steam-Done Sensor
new_elements: Steam/moisture sensor (Detects steam release as food heats.); Stops when food is hot (Ends cycle automatically at doneness signal.)
rationale: No timer guessing is required, supporting simple operation for.
judge_comment: Steam-based doneness detection eliminates timer guessing and is proven in sensor-cook models, though not very wild.

title: Voice-Only Microwave
new_elements: Offline voice command (Local speech recognition for basic commands.); Wake-word microphone (Listens for simple phrases like cook or open.)
rationale: Natural speech removes interface learning, directly serving.
judge_comment: Offline voice control removes the panel and learning, but it adds cost and complexity rather than substituting something simpler, and it is a fairly common concept.

title: Gesture Door
new_elements: Proximity/gesture door opener (Hand wave opens the door without touching.)
rationale: Opening the door becomes intuitive and touch-free, reducing steps for.
judge_comment: Touch-free door opening is intuitive but only covers opening the door, not the cooking operation, so it does little for the learning curve.

title: Foot Pedal Door
new_elements: Foot pedal latch release (A floor pedal opens the microwave door.)
rationale: Users operate by foot without learning a panel, serving and hands-full cooking.
judge_comment: A foot pedal is simple and mechanical, but it is awkward and only handles the door, so its relevance to M6 is limited.

title: Pull-Anywhere Door
new_elements: Magnetic push-pull latch (Door opens by pulling anywhere on its edge.)
rationale: Removes the need to find a small button, simplifying use for.
judge_comment: A magnetic pull-anywhere latch is a cheap, practical substitution for the button that eases door opening, but the change is incremental and not radical.

title: Tap-to-Add-30s
new_elements: Single tap button (Each tap adds a fixed 30 seconds.); Adds fixed increment (No dial or numeric entry needed.)
rationale: A single repeated action is instantly understood, strongly serving.
judge_comment: A single button that adds 30 seconds per tap replaces the keypad with the simplest possible action, which fits M6 and the substitute operator well, though similar buttons already exist.

title: Big Red Cook Button
new_elements: Large single cook button (One oversized button cycles common cook times.); Cycles preset times (Presses step through 1, 2, 3 minutes.)
rationale: The largest control is the only control, minimizing learning for.
judge_comment: Simple and feasible single-button design, but similar to existing +1 minute buttons and not radical.

title: Icon-Only Presets
new_elements: Six food icons (Pictograms for reheat, defrost, drink, popcorn, leftovers, frozen meal.); One-touch preset (Each icon sets time and power.)
rationale: No text or numbers are needed, making operation obvious for.
judge_comment: Pictogram presets are very intuitive and concrete, though common on existing microwaves.

title: Dial-Less Rotary Time
new_elements: One rotary encoder (Single knob only controls time.); Time only; power auto (Power is chosen automatically.)
rationale: Reduces two knobs to one familiar action, serving.
judge_comment: A single time knob with automatic power is familiar and easy, but only modestly novel.

title: Pull-Cord Timer
new_elements: Pull cord with spring return (Pull once for a standard cook duration.); Sets time by feel (Tactile cord returns to zero.)
rationale: Uses a single physical pull instead of dial reading, simplifying use for.
judge_comment: A pull cord is a novel, tactile interaction, but a single standard duration limits its usefulness and cord ergonomics are doubtful.

title: Hourglass Visual Timer
new_elements: Physical hourglass dial (Sand or beads visibly count down time.); Shows remaining time simply (No numbers or clock reading required.)
rationale: Intuitive visual countdown avoids digital-time learning for.
judge_comment: A visual hourglass countdown is intuitive and distinctive, but it is hard to make accurate and to link to the cook cycle.

title: Ambient Light Status
new_elements: Cavity LED ring (Ring glows to show on/off and progress.); Shows status by color (Color changes replace numbers.)
rationale: Status is understood without reading a control panel, serving.
judge_comment: Color-based status is easy to understand and plausible, but it only gives feedback and doesn't simplify input, and it isn't very radical.

title: Transparent Heated Door
new_elements: Transparent heated glass door (Whole door is see-through and stays clear.); No lamp needed to see (External light or ambient light shows food.)
rationale: Removes lamp use and makes viewing automatic, supporting simple operation for.
judge_comment: A fully transparent door is hard to reconcile with microwave shielding, and it does little for ease of operation.

title: Camera-to-Screen Door
new_elements: Door camera and OLED outer skin (Camera displays food on outer door screen.); Shows food without opening (No peering through holes or lamp.)
rationale: Users see cooking progress without touching controls, serving.
judge_comment: A camera feeding an outer OLED skin is novel and concrete, but it is costly and complex, and the heat and moisture inside are problems; it also doesn't simplify the controls.

title: Electroluminescent Walls
new_elements: EL cavity liner (Cavity walls glow evenly when powered.); Even glow without bulb (No replaceable lamp or hotspot.)
rationale: Illumination is automatic and maintenance-free, reducing user learning for.
judge_comment: EL walls would have trouble surviving microwave fields and heat, and illumination has little bearing on learning curve.

title: Aroma Signal
new_elements: Aroma release capsule (Releases a food-like scent when cooking ends.); Smell signals done (No bell or display interpretation needed.)
rationale: End-of-cook feedback is sensed naturally, requiring no learned signal for.
judge_comment: Scent as a done signal is highly original and intuitive, but capsules are consumable, unreliable and could be unpleasant, and the scent might not match the food.

title: Light Fade Alert
new_elements: Dimmable cavity light (Light pulses softly at end of cycle.); Light pulses at end (Visual alert replaces mechanical bell.)
rationale: A gentle visible signal is easier to understand than a bell, serving.
judge_comment: Easy to build, but it only changes the end-of-cycle alert and does little for the learning curve of operating the microwave.

title: Name-Call Voice Alert
new_elements: Voice announcer (Speaks the food name or simply says ready.); Says food is ready (Audible words replace cryptic ding.)
rationale: Plain-language feedback removes ambiguity, supporting.
judge_comment: Plain-language speech is clearer than a ding, but it only affects feedback and voice-enabled microwaves already exist.

title: Presence-Based Auto Door
new_elements: IR hand-wave sensor (Detects hand near door and opens it.); Door opens hands-free (No button press needed.)
rationale: Opening becomes automatic and intuitive, serving.
judge_comment: Hands-free opening is intuitive, but it does not address setting time or power, and it risks accidental opening.

title: Drawer Microwave
new_elements: Sliding drawer cavity (Food is placed on a pull-out drawer.); Push to close, pull to open (No hinged door or button.)
rationale: Drawer action is familiar from cabinets, eliminating door-button learning for.
judge_comment: A push-pull drawer is familiar and has been built commercially, but it still needs controls and has sealing and cost challenges.

title: Top-Loading Clamshell
new_elements: Top hinged lid (Lid flips up for drop-in access.); Drop food in, close (No side door or latch.)
rationale: Top loading is self-evident and simple, directly serving.
judge_comment: Top loading is self-evident, but spills, the interlock, and the lack of any control simplification limit its value for M6.

title: No Turntable Mode Stirrer
new_elements: Rotating mode stirrer (Metal vanes rotate in the waveguide to move the field.); Even heating without user-facing tray (Removes turntable alignment and cleaning.)
rationale: Removes turntable setup and alignment, simplifying every cook for.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers already exist in many microwaves, so this is feasible but not novel, and it only modestly helps the no-learning-curve need.

title: Auto-Rotating Antenna
new_elements: Rotating antenna (Antenna sweeps the cavity field electronically.); Field rotation no tray (Even heating without moving food.)
rationale: No turntable means no placement decisions, serving.
judge_comment: A rotating antenna is a real approach (rotating-antenna ovens exist), and it removes the turntable, though the benefit to ease of use is indirect.

title: Fixed Susceptor Turntable
new_elements: Self-centering susceptor tray (Tray drops into place with no roller ring.); No alignment needed (Magnetic or shaped seat centers itself.)
rationale: Removes the fiddly turntable alignment step, supporting.
judge_comment: A self-centering tray is plausible, but it is a minor tweak that does little for a no-learning-curve experience.

title: Magnetic Drop-In Tray
new_elements: Magnetic self-aligning tray (Tray snaps onto drive hub with magnets.); No roller ring (Eliminates loose parts and correct orientation.)
rationale: One-piece drop-in tray is easier to use and clean, serving.
judge_comment: A magnetic snap-on tray is concrete and easy to build, but it is a small improvement that is not radical.

title: Auto-Open Vapor Door
new_elements: Vapor/steam sensor door (Door pops open when cooking completes.); Opens when done (No user action needed at end.)
rationale: Removes the final door-opening decision, supporting hands-free simplicity for.
judge_comment: An auto-opening door is a distinctive hands-free idea, but it could cause safety and spill problems and it lacks detail on how it senses completion.

title: Smartphone Tap Cook
new_elements: NFC tap-to-cook (Phone tap transfers cook settings.); Phone app-less NFC tag (No app needed if phone supports NFC.)
rationale: Uses a familiar phone tap instead of microwave knobs, reducing learning for.
judge_comment: NFC tap is plausible and familiar, but it needs phone setup and a source of cook settings, so it is not truly zero-learning, and it doesn't clearly substitute a part.

title: Universal Meal Code
new_elements: QR code cook database (Camera reads QR code on packaging.); Camera (Integrated camera scans meal codes.)
rationale: Scanning a code is simpler than setting time and power, serving.
judge_comment: Scanning package codes is simple and feasible, but it depends on packaged food and a code database, and similar products already exist.

title: Thermal Camera Auto-Stop
new_elements: Thermal camera (Monitors surface temperature of food.); Stops at target temp (No timer entry needed.)
rationale: Cooking becomes automatic once started, serving.
judge_comment: A thermal camera replacing the timer gives automatic stopping, but it only senses surface temperature and adds cost, and the user still has to start it.

title: Weight + Steam Fusion
new_elements: Weight and humidity sensor (Combines mass and moisture data.); Auto cook any food (Chooses time and power without input.)
rationale: Eliminates all manual settings, making operation zero-learning for.
judge_comment: Sensor-based auto cooking removes all settings and fits the need best, though sensor cooking already exists and accuracy is hard to get right.

title: One-Knob Power/Time
new_elements: Push-turn knob (Press to cycle power, turn to set time.); Press for power, turn for time (One control replaces two.)
rationale: Reduces control count and keeps a familiar knob metaphor for.
judge_comment: A single push-turn knob is simple and easy to build, but it is incremental and not radical, and the press-to-cycle behavior still has to be learned.

title: Adaptive Defaults
new_elements: Learning default timer (Remembers the most-used setting.); Remembers last use (Next cook starts at same setting.)
rationale: Users repeat one action without re-setting, reducing cognitive load for.
judge_comment: Remembering the last setting is plausible and reduces effort, but it is not a substitution and could confuse users when the remembered default is wrong.

title: No Power Knob
new_elements: Fixed full-power only (Magnetron always runs at full power.); Simplifies to one control (Only time or preset is selected.)
rationale: Removing power selection removes an entire concept to learn, serving.
judge_comment: Dropping power selection cuts a concept and cost, but it makes delicate tasks worse and is a simple removal rather than a radical idea.

title: Auto-Defrost Button
new_elements: Dedicated defrost button (One button runs a complete defrost cycle.); One-touch defrost (No weight or time entry.)
rationale: Defrost becomes a single obvious action, directly serving.
judge_comment: One-touch defrost is a clear benefit, but it already exists on most microwaves, and without a weight input it cannot defrost reliably.

title: Reheat Only Button
new_elements: Reheat button (Starts a safe reheating cycle.); Ignores power levels (Automatically cycles power.)
rationale: The most common task needs only one button press, supporting.
judge_comment: A single reheat button suits the most common task and is feasible, but it is a familiar preset and the 'safe' outcome depends on sensing.

title: Beverage Button
new_elements: Beverage button (Heats a mug to a safe drinking temperature.); Heats drink to safe temp (No time or power entry.)
rationale: A single button for the most frequent breakfast task removes learning for.
judge_comment: A beverage button is intuitive and targets a frequent task, but reaching a safe drinking temperature needs a sensor, and the idea doesn't say how.

title: Popcorn Button
new_elements: Popcorn sensor (Listens for popping to stop at right time.); Listens for pops (No bag size or time entry.)
rationale: One-button popcorn with automatic stop is simple and predictable for.
judge_comment: Acoustic popcorn detection exists on some microwaves, so it is practical and simple but not radical, and it covers only one food.

title: Acoustic Doneness
new_elements: Microphone (Listens for boiling, sizzling, or popping.); Listens for doneness cues (Stops when sound signature matches.)
rationale: No timer setting is needed for common foods, serving.
judge_comment: Generalized acoustic doneness is novel and removes timer entry, but sound signatures vary widely and are unreliable for most foods.

title: Zero UI Always-On
new_elements: Presence sensor (Detects food placed and door closed.); Starts when food placed and door closed (Automatic cook cycle begins.)
rationale: The microwave operates with no interface at all, maximally serving.
judge_comment: Removing the interface is radical, but with no way to set power or time it risks overcooking or unsafe starts, and the cook parameters are undefined.

title: Door-Close Auto Start
new_elements: Lid switch (Closing the door triggers the last preset.); Closing door starts preset (No start button.)
rationale: Closing the door is the only required action, making use self-evident for.
judge_comment: Easy to build with the existing door switch, but starting on close risks accidental runs and repeated use of a stale preset.

title: Single Motion Cook
new_elements: Wave hand to start (Gestures start and stop cooking.); Gesture sensor (Detects simple hand motions.)
rationale: Simple gestures replace buttons and knobs, serving.
judge_comment: Gesture control is a gimmick that adds a learning step and is less intuitive than a button, though technically doable.

title: Accessible Tactile Dial
new_elements: Large tactile dial with clicks (Big detented dial with physical stops.); No vision needed (Clicked positions map to presets.)
rationale: Tactile fixed positions reduce learning and support for elderly users.
judge_comment: Detented preset dial is simple and effective but a familiar, not radical, substitution for buttons.

title: Elderly Simple Remote
new_elements: Two-button remote (Start and stop only, large buttons.); Start/stop only (No settings on remote.)
rationale: A two-button remote is instantly understood, serving.
judge_comment: A two-button remote is easy to understand but doesn't remove setting complexity on the microwave itself.

title: Voice Feedback Confirmation
new_elements: Voice confirmation (Speaks selected setting and completion.); Says setting and done (No display reading needed.)
rationale: Spoken feedback confirms operation without learning a display for.
judge_comment: Voice confirmation exists already and adds feedback rather than simplifying operation or substituting a part.

title: Auto-Clean Cycle Button
new_elements: Clean button (Runs a steam-cleaning cycle automatically.); Runs steam clean (No manual scrubbing knowledge.)
rationale: One-button cleaning removes another learning burden, supporting.
judge_comment: Steam-clean is tangential to cooking operation and does not address the learning curve for core use.

title: Self-Setting Frozen Meal
new_elements: Frozen meal shape sensor (Recognizes standard tray shape and size.); Recognizes tray and cooks (Automatically defrosts and heats.)
rationale: Placing a standard frozen meal is enough; no settings are needed, serving.
judge_comment: Tray recognition that auto-cooks directly removes settings, though reliability across varied meals is a challenge.

title: One-touch auto-cook button
new_elements: One-touch auto-cook button (Single large button replaces both timer and power knobs.); Preset algorithm for common foods (Automatically chooses duration and duty cycle.); Selects and starts cooking automatically (User only presses one button.)
rationale: Eliminates two knobs and all number interpretation, making operation a single press.
judge_comment: Very simple to use, but one-touch auto-cook is common and the preset algorithm must guess the food, so it is not radical.

title: Food-icon selector dial
new_elements: Food-icon selector dial (Dial with soup, plate, frozen meal icons only.); Mechanical preset cam (Each icon position sets time and power.); Sets duration and power from icon (Cooking settings are chosen by picture.)
rationale: Replaces abstract numbers with instantly recognizable food pictures, requiring no learning.
judge_comment: A mechanical cam dial with food icons is cheap, intuitive and concrete, but the idea is incremental.

title: Package barcode scanner
new_elements: Barcode scanner (Scans microwave meal package instructions.); Packaged-food cook-code lookup (Maps barcode to time and power.); Auto-sets time and power from package (No user setting required.)
rationale: Users just scan the food package instead of deciding time and power.
judge_comment: Scanning adds a step and a database dependency, and it only helps with packaged food.

title: RFID tray reader
new_elements: RFID tray reader (Reads smart microwaveable trays.); RFID cook instruction tag (Tray tag stores optimal cook cycle.); Sets cooking cycle from tray (Automatically configures microwave.)
rationale: Placing the food is the only step, so there is no control learning curve.
judge_comment: Placing the tray is the only step, but it needs proprietary smart trays and industry adoption, which makes it impractical.

title: Steam-sensor auto-stop
new_elements: Steam sensor (Detects moisture released by hot food.); Humidity-based doneness detection (Stops cooking when food is done.); Stops cooking when done (Replaces timer counting.)
rationale: Removes the need to choose or understand a cooking time.
judge_comment: Sensor-based doneness detection removes the need to choose a time, and some microwaves already offer it, though accuracy varies by food.

title: More/less rocker after auto-preset
new_elements: More/less rocker (Two-button adjust after automatic preset.); Adjusts doneness after auto preset (User only nudges result up or down.)
rationale: The only choice is more or less, an intuitive binary decision.
judge_comment: Simple and intuitive, but it adds to existing presets, is not very radical, and is vague on mechanism.

title: Weight-based automatic power
new_elements: Weight sensor in turntable (Measures food load automatically.); Load-cell auto power (Sets duty cycle from weight and food type.); Sets power automatically (No power knob needed.)
rationale: Removes an entire control dimension that users would otherwise have to learn.
judge_comment: Load-cell sensing removes the power-level decision, which is plausible and concrete, though food-type identification is still unresolved.

title: Push-to-open magnetic latch
new_elements: Magnetic push-to-open latch (Door opens by pushing or pulling, no separate button.); Permanent-magnet latch with interlock (Safe door holding and release.); Opens and closes door by push or pull (No release button to find.)
rationale: Door operation becomes as simple as opening a cabinet, with no button to locate.
judge_comment: A magnetic push-to-open latch is feasible and removes the hunt for the release button, but it only covers door opening.

title: Integrated door-edge pull
new_elements: Integrated door-edge pull (Door edge itself is the opening lever.); Cam-action edge release (Pulling the edge trips the latch.); Opens door by pulling edge (No separate push button.)
rationale: The door itself signals how to open it, eliminating the hidden-release-button problem.
judge_comment: A pull-edge door is already common on microwaves and clearly signals how to open it, so it adds little new.

title: Voice-activated door opener
new_elements: Voice-activated door opener (Motorized hinge responds to a spoken command.); Speech recognition plus servo (Recognizes simple open and close words.); Opens door hands-free (No physical control needed.)
rationale: A spoken command is familiar and requires no button learning.
judge_comment: Voice-controlled door opening is more complex and costly than a handle, and it solves a trivial problem rather than the cooking controls.

title: Voice-only cooking control
new_elements: Far-field microphone (Listens for simple cooking phrases.); Intent recognition for microwave commands (Maps phrases to time, power, and door actions.); Interprets spoken cooking command (User says what they want heated.)
rationale: Natural speech removes all knobs, buttons, and numeric displays.
judge_comment: Voice control removes the interface entirely, but it is fairly common in smart appliances and can fail in noisy kitchens or for users with speech difficulties.

title: Foot pedal start/cancel
new_elements: Foot pedal (Large pedal starts and stops cooking.); Starts and stops cooking (No hands required.)
rationale: A single pedal is physically obvious and avoids a complex control panel.
judge_comment: A pedal is simple and obvious, but it does not set time or power, so it only partly solves operation and is awkward to use.

title: NFC phone tap zone
new_elements: NFC phone tap zone (Tap phone once to send a preset.); Phone-configurable presets (Caregiver can set simple presets remotely.); Receives one-tap cook command (No onboard programming needed.)
rationale: A single tap replaces all microwave settings, with setup handled elsewhere.
judge_comment: One-tap presets are simple at the point of use, but they depend on a phone and on someone doing the setup first, which weakens the no-learning-curve goal.

title: Doneness twist dial
new_elements: Doneness twist dial (Twist from light to dark, no numbers.); Viscous-damped timer (Maps twist angle to cook duration.); Sets duration by feel (User twists until it feels right.)
rationale: Replaces numeric time with an intuitive more-or-less twist.
judge_comment: A numberless light-to-dark twist dial is intuitive and works without any learning, and it substitutes a simpler part for the keypad.

title: Auto-only power module
new_elements: Auto power module (Microwave always chooses power level.); Sets power without user input (No power knob visible.)
rationale: Removing the power control entirely eliminates an unnecessary user decision.
judge_comment: Dropping power selection cuts out a decision users have to make, but auto-power is already common and the idea gives few details on how it works.

title: Pictogram button trio
new_elements: Pictogram button trio (Three large buttons: defrost, reheat, cook.); Selects preset by picture (One press chooses a complete cycle.)
rationale: Three obvious icons require no manual or memorized sequences.
judge_comment: Very simple and easy to use, but it's basically existing preset buttons and not radical.

title: Steam-sensor timer replacement
new_elements: Steam sensor (Watches humidity inside cavity.); Humidity detection (Detects when food has heated through.); Stops at doneness (No time entry.)
rationale: Cooking stops by itself, so the user never sets a duration.
judge_comment: Steam sensors already exist in many microwaves, but they remove time entry well and are practical.

title: Thermal-camera doneness stop
new_elements: Thermal camera (Maps surface temperature of food.); Infrared food temperature mapping (Stops at target temperature.); Stops when target temperature reached (Time is automatic.)
rationale: The microwave judges doneness, removing time-setting from the user.
judge_comment: Thermal imaging for automatic doneness is more radical and fits the need, but it adds cost and has to cope with steam and a metal cavity.

title: Memory cook button
new_elements: Memory cook button (Repeats the last cooking cycle.); One-button repeat last setting (Stores previous time and power.); Repeats last cooking cycle (No new settings for repeated meals.)
rationale: For daily routines, one button repeats everything without relearning.
judge_comment: Easy and helpful for repeat use, but it does nothing for first-time use and is common already.

title: Push-turn combo knob
new_elements: Push-turn combo knob (Turn for time, press for power.); Sets duration and power with one control (Single physical control for both settings.)
rationale: One familiar knob replaces two separate controls, reducing confusion.
judge_comment: A familiar knob is easy to understand, but the turn-and-press modes add a little complexity and the idea is old.

title: Transparent EMI shielding window
new_elements: Transparent EMI shielding window (Clear film blocks microwaves without a visible mesh.); Indium tin oxide coating (Transparent conductive coating replaces perforated metal.); Blocks microwaves while transparent (Clean see-through door.)
rationale: A plain clear window looks simpler and removes the need to understand the mesh.
judge_comment: A clear window does little for operation simplicity, and ITO at microwave-blocking thickness and durability is questionable, though it is a concrete substitution.

title: No-turntable mode stirrer
new_elements: Mode stirrer (Rotating antenna distributes microwaves.); Distributes microwaves without turntable (No plate to place or align.)
rationale: Removing the turntable removes a setup step and alignment decision.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers already exist and removing the turntable does cut a part, but the gain in learning-curve terms is modest.

title: Flat no-align tray
new_elements: Flat no-align tray (Plain microwave-safe tray with no rotating coupling.); Holds food without alignment (Just place food anywhere.)
rationale: Users cannot misplace or misalign a turntable that is not there.
judge_comment: A flat tray without rotation gives uneven heating and barely affects operation simplicity.

title: Built-in rotating antenna
new_elements: Built-in rotating antenna (Hidden antenna replaces glass turntable.); Antenna stirring (Even heating without moving parts in the cavity.); Heats evenly without user setup (No turntable to clean or place.)
rationale: Even heating happens invisibly, so the user has one less part to manage.
judge_comment: It is essentially the same as the mode stirrer idea, a feasible and common approach that removes a user-managed part.

title: Shape-memory door pop
new_elements: SMA door pop (Door automatically pops open when cooking ends.); Shape-memory alloy actuator (Small heated wire releases latch.); Opens door automatically (No need to remember to open it.)
rationale: The microwave performs the final action, reducing steps for the user.
judge_comment: An automatic door pop on completion removes a step and is a plausible, concrete mechanism that suits a no-learning-curve goal.

title: Voice completion prompt
new_elements: Voice prompt (Speaks Done instead of just ringing.); Announces completion clearly (User knows when food is ready.)
rationale: A spoken status removes ambiguity about whether the cycle is finished.
judge_comment: Easy to build but only addresses end-of-cycle notification, not operation, and voice prompts are already common; it is not a substitution or radical.

title: Traffic-light progress ring
new_elements: Three-light progress ring (Green, yellow, red show remaining time.); Shows time remaining without numbers (No clock reading needed.)
rationale: Progress is understood at a glance without reading or interpreting digits.
judge_comment: Intuitive display substitution that helps at a glance, but it only affects feedback, not setting up the cook, and is modest in novelty.

title: Weight-aware twist dial
new_elements: Weight-aware twist dial (Dial combines weight sensing and timer.); Load cell plus cam timer (Sets duration from food weight.); Sets duration from weight (User only chooses a rough food size.)
rationale: The microwave calculates time, leaving only a simple twist.
judge_comment: Replaces the keypad and timer with a single weight-driven twist, which strongly removes the learning curve, though accuracy across foods is a challenge.

title: Moisture auto-power sensor
new_elements: Moisture sensor (Senses steam and adjusts power.); Adjusts power automatically (No power knob.)
rationale: Automatic power control removes a setting that many users never understand.
judge_comment: Removes the power setting via sensing, which is plausible and already partly present in sensor-cook models, but still leaves time setting.

title: Capacitive door-edge sensor
new_elements: Capacitive door-edge sensor (Touch the door edge to release latch.); Opens latch on touch (No push button.)
rationale: The whole door edge becomes the button, so there is nothing small to find.
judge_comment: Touch-to-open door is easy to use and a neat substitution for the button, but it carries accidental-opening risks and has a limited effect on the overall learning curve.

title: Gesture door opener
new_elements: Gesture sensor (Wave hand near door to open.); IR proximity and gesture (Detects simple hand wave.); Opens door hands-free (No contact needed.)
rationale: A wave is an intuitive gesture and avoids locating a release button.
judge_comment: Hands-free door opening is easy to use but only addresses the door, not the cooking operation, and a release button is already simple.

title: E-nose doneness stop
new_elements: E-nose (Gas sensor array detects cooking aromas.); Gas sensor array (Identifies when food aroma indicates done.); Stops when aroma indicates done (No time or power setting.)
rationale: The microwave cooks by sensing, so the user does not configure anything.
judge_comment: Aroma-based doneness would remove all settings, but gas sensors in a microwave cavity are unreliable and food-dependent.

title: Acoustic popcorn sensor
new_elements: Acoustic popcorn sensor (Listens for popcorn pops.); Stops when popping slows (Perfect popcorn without a time setting.)
rationale: A common microwave task becomes fully automatic and mistake-proof.
judge_comment: Acoustic popcorn sensing is plausible and some microwaves already do it, but it only covers one task.

title: Food camera auto-cycle
new_elements: Food camera (Camera looks at food before cooking.); Vision recognition (Identifies common foods and sets cycle.); Identifies food and sets cycle (No user input.)
rationale: The microwave recognizes the meal and configures itself automatically.
judge_comment: Camera recognition fully removes input, though accuracy and the need for power and time settings make it hard to execute.

title: Door-close auto-start
new_elements: Presence and weight sensor (Detects food and door closure.); Starts cooking on door close (No start button needed.)
rationale: Closing the door is the only action, so there is no control sequence to learn.
judge_comment: Starting on door close is simple and feasible, but without a time or power setting it risks unsafe or wrong cooking.

title: Door-close auto-start and open-stop
new_elements: Door-close auto-start (Starts cooking when door closes; opening stops it.); Starts on close, stops on open (Door movement is the only control.)
rationale: The physical door becomes the entire interface, which everyone already understands.
judge_comment: Door-as-interface is intuitive and plausible, but there is no way to set time or power, and the stop-on-open behavior is already how microwaves work; auto-start raises safety and accidental-start concerns.

title: Single defrost button
new_elements: Defrost button (One dedicated defrost preset.); Sets defrost power (No power knob.)
rationale: Defrost is reduced to one obvious button instead of a power-level decision.
judge_comment: Defrost buttons already exist on most microwaves, so this is trivial and only covers one function.

title: Recipe card slot
new_elements: Recipe card slot (Insert a card for a specific meal.); Mechanical code reader (Card holes encode time and power.); Sets time and power from card (No manual settings.)
rationale: Cards provide a physical, tactile way to avoid learning settings.
judge_comment: A mechanical card reader that encodes time and power is concrete and tactile, but it needs a card ecosystem and offers limited flexibility.

title: Color-coded preset buttons
new_elements: Color-coded preset buttons (Buttons match colors on food packaging.); Selects preset by color (No text or numbers.)
rationale: Color matching is pre-literate and requires no instruction.
judge_comment: Color matching removes the need for text, but it depends on packaging standards that don't exist and is limited to supported foods.

title: Guided one-button pulse
new_elements: Guided one-button (Illuminated button pulses when ready to press.); Prompts and starts cooking (The button shows exactly what to do.)
rationale: The interface actively guides the user to the only action needed.
judge_comment: A pulsing single button is very easy to use and feasible, but it is an incremental guidance idea that doesn't say how time or power get set.

title: Click-count timer
new_elements: Click-count timer (Each click adds one minute.); Sets duration by clicks (No dial numbers needed.)
rationale: Counting clicks is simpler than reading and setting a 0-30 minute dial.
judge_comment: Simple and feasible, but click-to-add-minute timers are already common and it's hardly radical or a true substitution.

title: Auto duty-cycle module
new_elements: Auto duty-cycle module (Microwave always uses optimal cycling.); Sets average power automatically (No power setting exposed.)
rationale: The machine hides power modulation, reducing the control panel to one action.
judge_comment: Hides power settings, but user still has to set time and the mechanism is vague; inverter microwaves already do this.

title: Leftover reheat button
new_elements: Leftover reheat button (One button reheats any plate safely.); Steam and IR sensor (Detects target temperature.); Reheats to safe target temperature (No time or power entry.)
rationale: The most common task becomes one button with automatic sensing.
judge_comment: One-button reheat serves the need well, but IR sensing of food temperature through steam is imperfect and similar features already exist.

title: Single START plus sensor fusion
new_elements: Single START button (Only control on the panel.); Sensor fusion auto-cook (Weight, steam, and IR sensors set time and power.); Starts automatic cooking (Cancel by opening door.)
rationale: One button and automatic sensing make the microwave usable with zero instruction.
judge_comment: A single START button with sensor fusion gives zero learning curve and is a bold simplification, though reliable auto-cooking for all foods is hard.

title: Rotary food doneness selector
new_elements: Rotary food doneness selector (Dial labeled warm, hot, crispy.); Selects doneness outcome (Internally sets time and power.)
rationale: Users choose the result they want, not the machine settings.
judge_comment: Outcome-based dial is intuitive and feasible, but labels like 'crispy' are ambiguous and the concept is a modest twist on preset buttons.

title: Automatic door-open chime
new_elements: Automatic door-open chime (Door pops and chimes when done.); Signals and enables access (No waiting for bell interpretation.)
rationale: The finished state is physically obvious because the door opens.
judge_comment: Practical and easy, but it only handles the end-of-cook signal, and many microwaves already beep and some open on a button press.

title: No-numbers countdown ring
new_elements: No-numbers countdown ring (LED ring shrinks as time passes.); Shows remaining time graphically (No digits to read.)
rationale: A shrinking ring communicates progress without any numeric literacy.
judge_comment: An LED ring communicates remaining time clearly, but it doesn't remove the need to set the time at the start.

title: Place-and-cook weight mat
new_elements: Place-and-cook weight mat (Mat senses food weight and starts preset.); Starts cooking based on placed food (No buttons or knobs.)
rationale: Placing food is the only action, eliminating the control panel.
judge_comment: Place-and-cook removes the controls entirely, but weight alone can't reliably identify food or the right program, and it's a safety concern.

title: Mechanical food-type wheel
new_elements: Mechanical food-type wheel (Wheel selects meat, veg, soup, frozen.); Sets preset from food type (No time or power entry.)
rationale: Food type is a familiar category, so users avoid abstract settings.
judge_comment: A food-type wheel is intuitive and replaces time and power entry, but similar presets already exist and it isn't very radical.

title: Tactile braille and icon panel
new_elements: Tactile braille and icon panel (Raised icons and braille labels on presets.); Guides selection by touch (No visual reading required.)
rationale: Touch-based labels reduce reliance on learning a visual control layout.
judge_comment: Tactile labels help accessibility and are easy to build, but they don't simplify the operation itself or reduce the learning curve much.

title: Single cancel-open bar
new_elements: Single cancel-open bar (Wide bar opens door and cancels cooking.); Stops cooking and opens door (One physical action for stop.)
rationale: Stopping is always the same obvious action, with no cancel button to find.
judge_comment: Simple and plausible, but it only addresses stopping rather than the whole operation, and microwaves already stop when the door opens.

title: Automatic microwave-safe meal detection
new_elements: Meal detection camera (Recognizes plate, bowl, and package shapes.); Shape and texture recognition (Chooses safe automatic cycle.); Detects meal type automatically (No user settings.)
rationale: The microwave identifies the meal and removes all setup decisions.
judge_comment: Camera-based meal recognition would remove nearly all setup decisions, but reliable heating without user input is hard and the idea adds cost instead of substituting something cheaper.

title: Pull-cord cooking command
new_elements: Pull-cord cooking command (Pull once to warm, twice to cook.); Starts simple warm or cook cycle (No panel learning.)
rationale: A pull-cord is a familiar mechanical interaction with only two meanings.
judge_comment: A pull-cord is an unusual and cheap mechanical substitute, but two fixed meanings give limited cooking control and may be unintuitive.

title: Open-door stop-only interface
new_elements: Open-door stop-only interface (No stop button; opening door always cancels.); Cancels cooking when door opens (One universal stop action.)
rationale: Users only need to remember that opening the door stops cooking.
judge_comment: This is how existing microwaves already behave, so it is feasible but barely new and covers only the stop action.

title: All-in-one cook dial
new_elements: All-in-one cook dial (Turn to time, machine selects power.); Sets duration with automatic power (Single dial operation.)
rationale: One dial is less confusing than separate timer and power controls.
judge_comment: A single dial that sets time and picks power automatically is very easy to use and cheap, but the idea is familiar and already common.

title: One-touch auto-cook
new_elements: One-touch auto-cook function (Replaces timer and power knobs with one button that runs a safe default cycle.)
rationale: A single button removes all settings decisions, so anyone can cook immediately.
judge_comment: Very simple and highly usable, but one-button microwaves already exist and it is not radical; the default cycle is vague.

title: Barcode-scan cook
new_elements: Barcode-scan cook function (Replaces manual time/power selection with a scanner that reads food packaging.)
rationale: Scanning a package eliminates learning any microwave controls.
judge_comment: Scanning packages is workable and somewhat novel, but it needs a database and does not help with food that has no barcode.

title: Voice-only cook
new_elements: Voice-only cook function (Replaces knobs and buttons with simple spoken commands like cook or stop.)
rationale: Speaking is a zero-learning interface for most users.
judge_comment: Voice control is intuitive and feasible, but it is already common and noisy kitchens or accents can cause failures.

title: Weight-sensing reheat
new_elements: Weight-sensing auto-reheat function (Replaces timer knob with a scale that chooses time and power automatically.)
rationale: Users just place food in and press one button, with no time calculation.
judge_comment: Weight sensing with auto-selected cooking is plausible and easy to use, but weight alone is an imperfect proxy for food type and heating needs.

title: Moisture-sensing stop
new_elements: Moisture-sensing stop function (Replaces the mechanical bell timer with a sensor that stops when food is done.)
rationale: No timer setting or guessing is needed to avoid overcooking.
judge_comment: Stopping automatically when the food is done removes all setting decisions and is a real substitute for the timer, though humidity sensors are imprecise.

title: Steam-pop done signal
new_elements: Steam-pop done signal function (Replaces the bell with a physical steam pop when moisture escapes.)
rationale: A simple audible pop requires no display or timer interpretation.
judge_comment: A steam pop is an intuitive done cue, but it's unreliable across foods and doesn't address operating the controls.

title: Transparent no-lamp door
new_elements: Transparent no-lamp visibility function (Replaces the interior lamp and door holes with a fully transparent shielding panel.)
rationale: Users can see food without operating a light or remembering to check.
judge_comment: A transparent shielding panel would help visibility, but a truly transparent panel can't block microwaves, and without a lamp the cavity would be dim.

title: Glow-in-dark cavity
new_elements: Glow-in-dark cavity visibility function (Replaces the lamp with phosphorescent cavity walls that charge from ambient light.)
rationale: Visibility is automatic, with no lamp switch or bulb to understand.
judge_comment: Phosphorescent walls are novel, but they would fade quickly, get dirty, and tolerate heat and moisture poorly; the benefit to operation is marginal.

title: Touchless wave-open
new_elements: Touchless wave-open function (Replaces the push-release button with a hand-wave sensor that opens the door.)
rationale: Opening the door becomes an intuitive gesture rather than a button press.
judge_comment: A wave sensor for opening the door is feasible and intuitive, but it adds cost, risks accidental triggers, and only covers door opening.

title: Foot-pedal door release
new_elements: Foot-pedal door release function (Replaces the push button with a large floor pedal.)
rationale: A pedal is obvious and usable without hands or learning labels.
judge_comment: A foot pedal is distinctive and obvious to use, but it's an awkward, impractical fit for a countertop microwave and doesn't simplify cooking operation.

title: Soft-close magnetic latch
new_elements: Soft-close magnetic latch function (Replaces the push-release latch with a magnet that opens and closes with a pull or push.)
rationale: The door behaves like a familiar cabinet, so no instruction is needed.
judge_comment: Makes the door familiar, but the door is a minor part of the learning curve and it doesn't address the controls.

title: Single-lever time/power
new_elements: Single-lever time/power function (Replaces both knobs with one lever: push to start, twist to add time.)
rationale: One physical control removes the confusion of separate timer and power knobs.
judge_comment: One lever consolidates the controls, though twist-to-add-time still needs some discovery and the change is modest.

title: Food-icon dial
new_elements: Food-icon dial function (Replaces numeric power levels with a dial showing pictures of common foods.)
rationale: Pictures are understood instantly without reading or learning power levels.
judge_comment: A pictorial dial is intuitive and easy to build, though food-to-power mapping is somewhat vague and not very radical.

title: Default two-minute start
new_elements: Default two-minute start function (Replaces the timer knob with a start button that always begins at two minutes.)
rationale: The most common reheat action requires no time entry at all.
judge_comment: Very simple, with zero learning for the common case, but it is an obvious solution and it limits flexibility.

title: Adaptive power
new_elements: Adaptive power function (Replaces the five-step power knob with automatic power modulation based on food load.)
rationale: Users no longer need to understand or choose power levels.
judge_comment: It removes the power decision entirely and is the most radical, but reliable load sensing is hard and the mechanism isn't described.

title: Temperature-target dial
