judge_comment: An RFID interlock is an overcomplicated replacement for a simple switch and does nothing for ease of use.

title: Static Mode Stirrer
new_elements: Static mode stirrer (Passive rotating vane in waveguide replaces turntable motor.); Even microwave distribution (Spreads microwaves without moving food.)
rationale: No turntable to place or align; user simply puts food in.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers are real and well established in commercial ovens, and they remove the turntable so users don't have to place food on it, though the benefit is modest.

title: Rotating Antenna
new_elements: Rotating antenna (Moves the microwave feed instead of the food.); Food-stationary heating (Heats evenly while plate stays still.)
rationale: Removes turntable placement decisions and cleaning complexity.
judge_comment: Rotating antennas exist in some commercial models and let the food sit still with no turntable alignment, but this does not directly simplify the controls.

title: Tilted Wave Reflector Tray
new_elements: Tilted reflector tray (Fixed angled tray scatters microwaves.); Stationary even heating (No rotating parts needed for uniformity.)
rationale: User never thinks about turntable orientation or alignment.
judge_comment: A stationary reflector or stirrer is plausible, and many microwaves already use one, but it only loosely serves a no-learning-curve goal.

title: Shaking Base
new_elements: Piezo shaking base (Vibrates food slightly instead of rotating it.); Agitation for even heating (Moves food minimally to avoid hot spots.)
rationale: No turntable to center; any placement is fine.
judge_comment: A piezo shaking base is novel, but it is unlikely to move heavy food enough, and it risks spills and noise, so it is a weak turntable replacement.

title: Transparent Door Casing
new_elements: Transparent shielded door (Full see-through door with embedded mesh replaces window and lamp.); Natural visual monitoring (User sees food without a lamp.)
rationale: Seeing inside is automatic; no light switch or guessing to learn.
judge_comment: A see-through door is already the norm, and removing the lamp would hurt visibility, so it adds little for ease of operation.

title: Phone Camera Interior View
new_elements: Cavity camera (Phone-viewable camera replaces window and lamp.); Remote visual check (User checks food on phone without opening door.)
rationale: Familiar phone screen replaces peering through a small window.
judge_comment: A cavity camera is feasible but adds a phone and app step, which cuts against the no-learning-curve need.

title: Transparent Conductive Mesh Door
new_elements: Transparent conductive mesh (Fine metal mesh replaces traditional perforated choke plate.); RF containment with clarity (Blocks microwaves while staying highly transparent.)
rationale: Makes the whole door a clear, obvious window with no hidden components.
judge_comment: A transparent conductive mesh door is technically plausible and concrete, but it has only a marginal effect on operating simplicity.

title: Fully Transparent Microwave Casing
new_elements: Transparent shielded casing (Entire outer shell is see-through and RF-safe.); All-around visibility (User sees food from any angle.)
rationale: No need to learn where the window is; the whole appliance is visible.
judge_comment: A transparent RF-safe shell is radical but physically implausible, since the shielding must be conductive and the window is not the real learning barrier.

title: Electroluminescent Interior Film
new_elements: Electroluminescent film (Glowing interior liner replaces incandescent lamp.); Soft cavity illumination (Even light with no bulb to replace.)
rationale: Always-on simple visibility without a separate lamp control.
judge_comment: An electroluminescent liner is a plausible lamp substitute, but it does almost nothing for ease of operation and must survive heat and microwaves.

title: LED Ring Light
new_elements: LED ring light (Ring of LEDs replaces incandescent bulb.); Shadow-free visibility (Lights food evenly for easy checking.)
rationale: Brighter, simpler visibility means less guesswork.
judge_comment: LED lighting is feasible and already common, and it only marginally helps operation.

title: Hydrophobic Ceramic Waveguide Cover
new_elements: Hydrophobic ceramic cover (Self-cleaning ceramic replaces mica sheet.); Splatter resistance (Grease and food slide off, keeping waveguide clear.)
rationale: Less cleaning and maintenance means simpler everyday operation.
judge_comment: A hydrophobic ceramic waveguide cover is a practical mica substitute, but it addresses maintenance rather than learning curve.

title: Automatic Bleeder Resistor
new_elements: Bleeder resistor (Permanently drains HV capacitor after use.); Automatic HV discharge (Removes lethal charge without service action.)
rationale: Safety becomes invisible and automatic, with no user learning.
judge_comment: Bleeder resistors are already standard in microwaves, so this is neither new nor relevant to ease of use.

title: Solid-State HV Module
new_elements: Solid-state HV module (Integrated block replaces discrete diode and doubler.); Plug-in high voltage (Provides magnetron power with fewer user-visible parts.)
rationale: Simplifies internal architecture so operation stays one-button reliable.
judge_comment: An internal HV architecture change that users never see, so it barely affects learning curve.

title: Inverter HV Supply
new_elements: Inverter HV supply (Variable high-frequency drive replaces transformer and doubler.); Continuous power control (Allows smooth power without duty-cycle cam.)
rationale: Replaces confusing duty-cycle power steps with smooth automatic control.
judge_comment: Inverter microwaves already exist; smooth power control removes some power-level choices but the user-facing benefit is indirect.

title: Digital One-Button Timer
new_elements: One-button digital timer (Single press increments by intuitive amounts.); Simple countdown setting (No numbers or power pairing needed.)
rationale: One button replaces a precise-looking but confusing mechanical timer.
judge_comment: A one-button timer is simple and plausible but is a conventional, non-radical idea that is limited in function.

title: Temperature Probe Auto Cook
new_elements: Wireless food probe (Stab probe measures internal temperature.); Probe-driven stop (Cooks until target temperature is reached.)
rationale: User inserts probe and presses start; no time or power knowledge needed.
judge_comment: Probe-driven cooking removes the need for time and power knowledge, though inserting a probe is an extra step and probes already exist.

title: Single Reheat Algorithm
new_elements: Universal reheat algorithm (One algorithm covers most leftovers.); Reheat button (Single dedicated button replaces power and time choices.)
rationale: Reheating is the most common task and becomes a single obvious button.
judge_comment: A single reheat button is highly intuitive, but it is already common and one algorithm will not suit every food.

title: Hall-Sensor Interlock Logic
new_elements: Hall-sensor interlock logic (Magnetic hall sensors replace three microswitches.); Fail-safe door sensing (Detects door state redundantly without mechanical switches.)
rationale: Safety is automatic and silent, with no switch feel to learn.
judge_comment: Technically plausible substitution, but it is invisible to the user and does almost nothing for operational simplicity.

title: Inductive Power Coupling
new_elements: Inductive power pad (Wireless power coupling replaces mains cord.); Place-and-power (Microwave powers by sitting on a counter pad.)
rationale: No plug orientation or cord management for simple setup.
judge_comment: Wireless power at roughly 1kW is impractical and inefficient, and it barely affects the learning curve of operating the microwave.

title: USB-C PD Low-Power Mode
new_elements: USB-C PD input (Low-power mode for reheating small items.); Cord-free simple power (Uses familiar USB-C cable for light duty.)
rationale: Uses a universally familiar connector, reducing setup learning.
judge_comment: USB-C PD tops out around 100-240W, which is too low to heat food well, and it does not address operation.

title: Aroma Release Done Signal
new_elements: Aroma release capsule (Releases a food-like smell when done.); Olfactory done signal (Signals completion through smell instead of bell.)
rationale: Smell is an intuitive, zero-learning completion cue.
judge_comment: An olfactory done signal is intuitive and original, but capsules are consumable and it only covers the completion cue.

title: Spring-Twist Timer
new_elements: Spring-twist timer (One spring mechanism combines start and duration.); Single-motion timing (Twist to both start and set time.)
rationale: One physical motion replaces separate power and timer setup.
judge_comment: A single twist that starts the cook and sets the time is a mechanical-timer approach that directly removes the learning curve and is easy to build.

title: Voice Command Control
new_elements: Voice command module (Simple wake word and cook commands.); Spoken operation (User says cook or stop without touching controls.)
rationale: Speaking is a natural interface requiring almost no appliance learning.
judge_comment: Voice control is a natural, low-learning interface, but it is a common feature and doesn't say how time or power get set.

title: Gesture Sensor Control
new_elements: Gesture sensor (Wave or swipe controls start and stop.); Touchless operation (Simple hand motions replace knobs.)
rationale: A wave is intuitive and avoids small-button confusion.
judge_comment: Waving is intuitive, but the idea doesn't explain how cook time or power are chosen, and accidental triggers are a risk.

title: One-Button Smartphone App
new_elements: Phone app bridge (App shows one large cook button.); Familiar app control (Uses phone UI patterns instead of appliance panel.)
rationale: Users already know their phone, so the microwave adds no new interface.
judge_comment: It's easy to build, but needing a phone and app setup adds learning steps and is more complex than a button.

title: NFC Tap-to-Cook
new_elements: NFC tap zone (Tap phone to send a cook command.); Tap-based operation (No panel navigation, just one tap.)
rationale: Tap is a simple, familiar gesture that replaces knob turning.
judge_comment: Tapping is simple, but it needs a phone and a preset command, so it doesn't clearly beat a Start button.

title: Voice-Open Door
new_elements: Voice door actuator (Voice command opens door latch.); Hands-free opening (Door pops open on spoken command.)
rationale: No need to find or push a release button.
judge_comment: It only covers opening the door, which is a minor part of operation, and the actuator adds cost and a safety concern.

title: Passive Convection Turntable Replacement
new_elements: Passive convection vane (Heat-driven air movement replaces turntable motor.); Gentle air circulation (Even heating without rotating plate.)
rationale: Removes turntable setup and still keeps heating simple.
judge_comment: Passive vane is physically implausible for microwave heating and doesn't much reduce operational complexity, though it does remove the turntable.

title: Phosphorescent Interior Coating
new_elements: Phosphorescent liner (Glow-in-the-dark cavity coating replaces lamp.); Passive visibility (Interior glows softly after door opens.)
rationale: No lamp, no switch, no thought; visibility is automatic.
judge_comment: Phosphorescent liner is cheap and simple but the glow would be weak and the lamp isn't a learning barrier, so relevance is low.

title: AR Projection Window
new_elements: AR projection window (Door glass projects simple cook status and food view.); Overlaid guidance (Shows one clear cue without panel reading.)
rationale: The door itself tells the user what to do, requiring no manual.
judge_comment: Projection on the door is novel but adds complexity and cost and still requires interpreting cues, with heat and glass issues.

title: Zero-Control Auto-Detect Microwave
new_elements: Auto-detect cooking (Detects food type, mass, and doneness automatically.); No-control cavity (No timer, power knob, or start button.)
rationale: There is literally nothing to learn; close door and it cooks.
judge_comment: Perfectly meets zero learning curve, but reliable automatic food and doneness detection is hard and there is no override or safety control.

title: Single Lever Cook/Open
new_elements: Single lever (One lever opens door and starts cooking.); Combined open-start action (Pulling lever opens; pushing closes and starts.)
rationale: One lever replaces door button, timer, and power controls.
judge_comment: A single lever combining open and start is simple and mechanically feasible, though cook duration and power are unspecified.

title: One-Touch Cook Button
new_elements: Single capacitive cook button (One large button that starts a safe default cook cycle.); Infers time and power from one press (Uses cavity load sensing to choose time and power automatically.)
rationale: Replaces two knobs with a single obvious action so there is nothing to learn.
judge_comment: A single button is highly relevant to zero learning, but load sensing to infer time and power is vague and only moderately reliable; one-touch start already exists.

title: Package-Scanning Microwave
new_elements: NFC/RFID food package tag reader (Reads smart package tags to get cooking instructions.); Automatically sets cook cycle (Translates package tag data into microwave settings.)
rationale: Users just tap the package, eliminating manual time and power decisions.
judge_comment: Tapping a package is simple, but it depends on smart package tags that barely exist, and it fails for leftovers and unlabeled food.

title: Weight-Sensing Auto-Cook
new_elements: Load cell under turntable (Weighs food inside the cavity.); Auto-selects power and time by mass (Maps weight to a safe heating profile.)
rationale: The microwave decides settings from the food's weight, so no learning is needed.
judge_comment: A load cell is feasible and concrete, but weight alone does not determine the right cook profile, and the idea is not radical.

title: Steam-Sensing Doneness Stop
new_elements: Humidity/steam sensor (Detects when food is releasing moisture rapidly.); Stops cooking at doneness (Ends cycle automatically instead of using a timer.)
rationale: Replaces timer judgment with automatic doneness detection.
judge_comment: Humidity sensors are proven in existing sensor-cook modes and remove timer guesswork, so this is practical but not new.

title: Sniff-and-Heat Aroma Sensor
new_elements: Volatile organic compound sensor (Smells food aromas as they develop.); Detects when food is hot enough (Triggers shutoff when aroma profile peaks.)
rationale: Users can walk away; the microwave knows by smell when to stop.
judge_comment: A VOC aroma sensor is more novel, but it is unreliable in a hot, humid cavity and a doneness signal from aroma is questionable.

title: Voice-Only Operation
new_elements: Always-on wake-word microphone (Listens for a single command such as 'warm it'.); Executes simple voice intents (Maps short phrases to heating cycles.)
rationale: No knobs or menus: the user says one phrase.
judge_comment: Voice control directly removes menus and is plausible, though common in smart appliances and not very radical.

title: Gesture Wave to Start
new_elements: IR proximity/gesture sensor (Detects a hand wave in front of the door.); Starts default warm cycle (One wave begins a safe reheat.)
rationale: Replaces button presses with an instinctive wave.
judge_comment: A wave to start a default cycle is intuitive and cheap, but accidental triggers and lack of food-amount control are risks.

title: Touchless Door by Foot
new_elements: Foot-operated kick latch (A pedal at floor level opens the door.); Hands-free door opening (User can open with a foot while holding food.)
rationale: Substitutes the push button with a foot action for simpler, mess-free use.
judge_comment: Foot-opening is convenient but addresses only door opening, not the core operation of choosing and starting a cycle.

title: Drawer-Slide Door
new_elements: Drawer-style sliding cavity (Pulls out like a drawer instead of swinging a door.); Direct drop-in loading (Food is placed down, not maneuvered into a box.)
rationale: Replaces the door button and swing with an obvious drawer motion.
judge_comment: A drawer motion is intuitive and has precedent in drawer microwaves, but it doesn't simplify the controls.

title: Transparent Microwave Casing
new_elements: Fully transparent RF-shielded casing (See-through mesh composite body.); See inside without lamp (Ambient light reveals the food.)
rationale: Removes the need to operate anything just to check food.
judge_comment: A transparent shielded body is eye-catching, but it barely helps operation and has RF-shielding and safety challenges.

title: OLED Status Window
new_elements: Transparent OLED door panel (Shows words and icons over the food.); Guides user with one icon (Displays a single relevant action.)
rationale: Replaces cryptic labels with obvious on-glass prompts.
judge_comment: Transparent OLED on a microwave door is novel and guides users, but heat, shielding and cost make it hard, and it is more complex rather than a substitution.

title: Food-Icon Rotary Dial
new_elements: Picture-only rotary dial (Dial shows pizza, soup, leftovers, drink.); Selects preset by picture (No words or numbers required.)
rationale: Substitutes numeric power/time with universally understood icons.
judge_comment: A picture-only dial is plausible and cheap and removes numeric entry, though presets like this already exist.

title: Single Chicken-Button Preset
new_elements: Dedicated reheat button (One button for the most common task.); Runs safe reheat profile (Uses a fixed conservative cycle.)
rationale: One dedicated action removes all mode confusion.
judge_comment: A single reheat button is simple and feasible but limited in function and not very radical; the name 'chicken' is also inconsistent with the description.

title: Popcorn-Only Appliance
new_elements: Single-purpose popcorn microwave (Only makes popcorn safely and perfectly.); One-button popcorn cycle (Fixed time and power for popcorn.)
rationale: Radical simplification: the product only does one obvious thing.
judge_comment: A popcorn-only microwave is radically simple but too narrow, and it exists as a niche concept.

title: Magnetic Door Snap
new_elements: Magnetic self-closing latch (Door snaps shut without a push button.); One-motion loading (Close door and it is ready.)
rationale: Removes the separate door-release button from the user's mental model.
judge_comment: A magnetic self-closing latch is feasible and removes a step, but it addresses only the door, and safety interlocks must be maintained.

title: Auto-Door Suction Seal
new_elements: Vacuum-assisted auto seal (Door pulls itself closed against a soft gasket.); No latch operation (User only pushes the door shut.)
rationale: Eliminates latch mechanics from the interaction.
judge_comment: Simplifies door closing, but microwave doors are already easy; it barely addresses the learning curve of operation.

title: RFID Plate Recognition
new_elements: RFID dish/container tagging (Plates contain passive tags with cooking profiles.); Auto-cooks for tagged dish (Microwave reads the dish and selects cycle.)
rationale: No settings are chosen because the dish itself tells the microwave what to do.
judge_comment: Tagged dishes remove settings entirely, but they require a proprietary dish ecosystem and don't work for arbitrary food.

title: Camera Food Recognition
new_elements: In-cavity food camera with AI (Identifies food type and amount.); Chooses cook program automatically (Maps recognized food to a preset.)
rationale: The user just puts food in; the appliance sees and decides.
judge_comment: Camera-based recognition directly enables zero-input operation and is already emerging in products, though it's less radical.

title: Lidar Portion Sizing
new_elements: Time-of-flight portion scanner (Measures height and volume of food.); Sets time by volume (Uses portion size to choose duration.)
rationale: Replaces manual time estimation with automatic portion measurement.
judge_comment: Volume alone ignores food type and composition, so it only partly automates cooking, though it does remove time guessing.

title: Thermal-Camera Doneness
new_elements: Infrared thermal camera (Reads surface temperature map of food.); Stops at target temperature (Ends cycle when food is warm enough.)
rationale: No timer setting: the microwave watches temperature and stops.
judge_comment: Stopping on surface temperature removes the timer, but it is limited by surface-only readings and uneven heating; the mechanism is clear.

title: Boil-Detecting Auto Stop
new_elements: Acoustic boil sensor (Listens for boiling signature.); Stops before superheating (Cuts power when water boils.)
rationale: Removes the need to learn safe liquid heating times.
judge_comment: Auto-stop on boil removes the need to guess liquid heating times and prevents superheating, though acoustic detection in a noisy microwave is technically challenging.

title: Mute Haptic Timer
new_elements: Haptic vibration puck (Vibrates instead of ringing a bell.); Non-audio completion signal (Signals done through touch.)
rationale: Substitutes the bell with an intuitive touch cue.
judge_comment: A haptic puck is a plausible swap for the bell, but it improves only the completion alert and does little for operating simplicity.

title: Countdown Color Ring
new_elements: Circular LED progress ring (Color ring around door shows remaining time.); Shows progress without numbers (Users understand time remaining at a glance.)
rationale: Replaces numeric timer reading with an obvious visual countdown.
judge_comment: An LED progress ring is easy to build and glanceable, but it only displays time and does not simplify setting it.

title: Traffic-Light Doneness
new_elements: Red-yellow-green status light (Simple three-color doneness indicator.); Communicates hot/cold state (No words or numbers.)
rationale: Uses universal traffic-light logic instead of a timer display.
judge_comment: Traffic-light status is intuitive, but it is unclear how the microwave would sense doneness, and the idea names no mechanism.

title: Smiley Face Done Screen
new_elements: E-ink smiley indicator (Shows a smile when food is ready.); Emotional done signal (No reading required.)
rationale: Substitutes timer digits with an instantly understood face.
judge_comment: A smiley done indicator is simple but trivial, and e-ink is a poor fit for a signal that must be seen while cooking.

title: Always-On Keep-Warm Mode
new_elements: Automatic keep-warm after cook (Holds food at safe serving temperature.); Low-duty thermostat control (Uses existing thermostat to pulse low power.)
rationale: Removes the need to reheat again if the user is not prompt.
judge_comment: Keep-warm is common and only marginally helps simplicity; it also doesn't really substitute a part.

title: Cold-Food Auto Start
new_elements: Door-close weight trigger (Detects food placed and door closed.); Starts warming automatically (Begins a gentle cycle without user input.)
rationale: The simplest possible operation: close the door and it works.
judge_comment: Auto-start on door close is very simple to use, but it risks unsafe or unwanted starts and it is unclear how the cook time or power is chosen.

title: Auto-Detect Empty Cavity
new_elements: Cavity load detector (Prevents running when empty.); No accidental empty start (User cannot make a confusing mistake.)
rationale: Removes a common error state so operation stays simple.
judge_comment: An empty-run guard is sensible and feasible, but it prevents a mistake rather than simplifying operation, and it is not a substitution.

title: Self-Cleaning Steam Cycle
new_elements: One-touch steam cleaning (Automated cleaning cycle.); Water reservoir cleaning puck (Adds water and runs steam.)
rationale: Reduces maintenance learning by making cleaning a single obvious action.
judge_comment: It addresses cleaning rather than operating the microwave, and steam-clean cycles already exist.

title: Splatter-Shield Consumable
new_elements: Disposable splatter film (Peel-off sheet protects waveguide cover.); No cleaning of mica cover (User replaces film instead of cleaning.)
rationale: Substitutes cleaning know-how with a simple replaceable part.
judge_comment: It is a true substitution of a consumable for cleaning, but it is tangential to operation and a film in the cavity is a concern near microwaves.

title: Edible Microwave Tray
new_elements: Edible wafer tray (Single-use tray holds food and is eaten or composted.); No turntable cleaning (Tray can be discarded after use.)
rationale: Replaces the turntable with a consumable so there is nothing to learn about cleaning.
judge_comment: Edible tray is wild but barely addresses simple operation, and it raises microwave safety and practicality issues.

title: Smartphone Tap-to-Cook
new_elements: NFC tap-to-cook pad (Phone taps microwave to send cook program.); Uses phone as remote control (User chooses food in a familiar app.)
rationale: Replaces on-device controls with a device the user already knows.
judge_comment: NFC tap-to-cook is highly feasible, but it needs a phone and an app, and many such products already exist.

title: QR Recipe Cook
new_elements: QR code scanner (Scans a recipe QR for exact settings.); Loads recipe automatically (No manual programming.)
rationale: Substitutes typing or dialing with scanning a code.
judge_comment: Scanning a QR code for settings works, but it adds steps and a camera, and some existing products already do it.

title: Cooking-by-Colour Cards
new_elements: Colour-coded recipe cards (Cards are placed on a reader.); Sets cycle by card colour (No numbers or words.)
rationale: Physical picture cards avoid any learning curve.
judge_comment: Wordless colour cards on a reader are intuitive and fairly novel, though the cards could get lost and limit flexibility.

title: Toy-Dial Big Knob
new_elements: Oversized child-like knob (One huge knob with only three positions.); Three obvious heat levels (Low, medium, high only.)
rationale: Reduces control choices to three intuitive levels.
judge_comment: One huge three-position knob is nearly zero-learning and easy to build, though it gives coarse control and is less radical.

title: Pull-Cord Start
new_elements: Pull-cord actuator (Pulling a cord starts a default cycle.); Mechanical one-pull start (No electronics UI.)
rationale: Substitutes knobs with a single familiar mechanical gesture.
judge_comment: A single pull gesture is simple and intuitive, though a mechanical start still needs a timer and safety interlock, and a default cycle may not suit every food.

title: Clap-On Microwave
new_elements: Clap-detection circuit (Listens for a double clap.); Starts or stops with claps (No buttons touched.)
rationale: A universally understood sound action replaces control panels.
judge_comment: Clap control is easy to understand, but false triggers from kitchen noise and the unsafe chance of starting an empty microwave undermine it.

title: Presence-Detect Auto Warm
new_elements: Human presence radar (Detects when a person is in the kitchen.); Pre-warms when user arrives (Starts warming a placed meal.)
rationale: The microwave acts before the user has to operate anything.
judge_comment: Zero-operation is appealing, but auto-starting heating based on presence is risky and unreliable, and it does not know what food is inside.

title: Schedule-by-Sunlight
new_elements: Ambient light sensor (Detects daylight and meal-time patterns.); Suggests warm cycle (Uses light level as simple context.)
rationale: Context-based defaults reduce user decisions.
judge_comment: Light level is a weak proxy for meal context, and it only suggests a cycle instead of simplifying operation.

title: Sunlight-Powered Display
new_elements: Photovoltaic e-ink label (No battery; shows simple status.); Zero-maintenance status (Always shows one symbol.)
rationale: Removes confusing displays and power switches from operation.
judge_comment: A solar e-ink label is feasible and removes some display complexity, but it barely helps the user operate the microwave.

title: Mechanical Bell Replacement with Voice
new_elements: Tiny voice chip (Says 'done' in plain language.); Spoken completion cue (No interpretation of bell needed.)
rationale: Substitutes an ambiguous ding with an explicit word.
judge_comment: Easy to build and clear, but it only simplifies the end-of-cycle cue and leaves the main operation untouched.

title: Single Power Button with Auto-Time
new_elements: One power button (Only turns on; time is automatic.); Eliminates timer setting (Uses default short-burst cycles.)
rationale: Removes the imprecise mechanical timer from the interaction.
judge_comment: A one-button microwave is very simple to use, but fixed short bursts may not suit varied foods, and the time-setting step is removed without a real substitute.

title: Auto-Reheat Leftovers Sensor
new_elements: Leftover reheat mode (Detects plate shape and assumes leftovers.); Plate-shape recognizer (Camera identifies a plated meal.)
rationale: The most common student task becomes automatic.
judge_comment: A camera that recognizes plated leftovers and sets reheat automatically cuts down on operation, but it is complex and may misclassify food, so it is not a cheaper substitution.

title: Frozen-Meal Auto-Detect
new_elements: Ice-crystal radar (Detects frozen food texture.); Selects defrost then cook (No user knows defrost settings.)
rationale: Removes the two-stage defrost-then-cook learning burden.
judge_comment: Auto-detecting frozen food and sequencing defrost then cook removes a real learning burden, but radar-based ice detection is hard and costly.

title: No-Power-Knob Duty-Cycle Chip
new_elements: Fixed duty-cycle driver (Always uses optimal pulse pattern.); No power selection (Power is not a user choice.)
rationale: Substitutes the five-step power knob with automatic power control.
judge_comment: Removing the power knob is simple and cheap, but it takes away user control and addresses only one part of operation.

title: Door-Handle Cook Trigger
new_elements: Handle-integrated start sensor (Closing the handle starts cooking.); Door close equals start (No separate start button.)
rationale: Replaces separate door latch and start actions with one motion.
judge_comment: Closing the door to start is plausible and intuitive, but there is no time or power setting and it is already partly standard, so it only partially fits the 'wild' brief.

title: Push-to-Open and Cook
new_elements: Push-to-open spring door (Push door once to open; push shut to cook.); Single push interaction (All user action is pushing the door.)
rationale: The door is the only control, so nothing needs learning.
judge_comment: Using the door as the sole control is simple, but it needs a default cook time and the push-to-cook logic is ambiguous.

title: Throw-Away HV Safety Module
new_elements: Sealed discharge resistor module (Permanently bleeds HV charge.); No user HV awareness (Safety is invisible and automatic.)
rationale: Removes a hidden dangerous concept from the user's mental model.
judge_comment: Bleeder resistors already exist and users never interact with them, so this does little for operational simplicity.

title: Arc-Proof Cavity Liner
new_elements: Metal-tolerant ceramic liner (Detects and extinguishes arcing.); Safe with accidental metal (User does not need to remember rules.)
rationale: Removes the need to learn the metal prohibition.
judge_comment: Metal-tolerant cooking would remove a real rule users must learn, but a ceramic liner that detects and extinguishes arcing is physically doubtful.

title: Child-Proof One-Button Lock
new_elements: Automatic safe lockout (Locks out complex modes by default.); Single unlock-and-cook button (One press does both.)
rationale: Even safety locks become one obvious action.
judge_comment: A default lockout with a single unlock-and-cook button is feasible and simple, but it is incremental and adds a lock concept.

title: Mechanical Timer as Single Egg-Timer
new_elements: Sand-timer visual dial (Analog sand timer shows short intervals.); Intuitive short-time heating (No numeric precision needed.)
rationale: Substitutes the imprecise timer with a visual short-time sand timer.
judge_comment: A sand-timer dial is simple and intuitive, but it only covers short intervals and isn't a real substitution that serves most cooking.

title: Mechanical Timer as 30-Minute Dial
new_elements: Detented 30-minute dial (Snaps only to 1, 5, and 10 minutes.); Limited choices reduce error (Prevents impossible settings.)
rationale: Fewer timer positions make operation obvious.
judge_comment: A detented dial with few positions is very easy to use, but it is an ordinary mechanical timer and the description is inconsistent (30-minute dial that snaps only to 1, 5 and 10).

title: Magnetron as Solid-State Heater
new_elements: Solid-state RF heating array (No warm-up or HV capacitor.); Instant precise heating (No power cycling guesswork.)
rationale: Substitutes complex HV with instantly controllable heat.
judge_comment: Solid-state RF is a real and radical technology swap, but it is not clearly tied to a no-learning-curve interface and is still costly.

title: Door Window as Touch Surface
new_elements: Capacitive door glass touch surface (The window itself is the control.); Touch food picture to cook (User taps a food icon on the glass.)
rationale: Replaces separate control panel with the window the user already looks at.
judge_comment: Using the door glass as a touch surface with food icons is intuitive and removes the control panel, though it needs a transparent touch layer plus RF shielding.

title: Door Window as Barcode Reader
new_elements: In-window barcode camera (Reads food package barcodes through glass.); Scans package to cook (No buttons pressed.)
rationale: Substitutes manual settings with showing the package to the window.
judge_comment: Showing a package to a barcode camera needs no buttons and is technically plausible, but it depends on a cooking-instruction database and fails for unpackaged food.

title: Microwave as Smart Speaker
new_elements: Alexa/Google built-in voice assistant (User says common cooking phrases.); Conversational cooking control (No new interface to learn.)
rationale: Uses an interface many users already know instead of microwave controls.
judge_comment: Voice control is a familiar interface and plausible, but it's an existing concept and doesn't solve how long to cook or loading, and it adds more than it substitutes.

title: Microwave as Phone Charger
new_elements: Qi wireless charging top (Top surface charges a phone.); Dual-purpose appliance (No extra learning: just place phone.)
rationale: A familiar phone-charging action makes the appliance feel simpler.
judge_comment: Phone charging does nothing to simplify microwave operation, and a hot, microwave-emitting top is a poor place for Qi charging.

title: Self-Opening Robot Door
new_elements: Motorized auto-door (Door opens when a hand approaches.); No touching door (User only places food.)
rationale: Replaces the door button and latch with automatic hospitality.
judge_comment: Auto-opening door is easy to build but removes only a trivial step and leaves the timer and power settings unaddressed.

title: Robotic Arm Loader
new_elements: Mini robot loading arm (Takes food from a tray into cavity.); Hands-free loading (User never opens or closes door.)
rationale: Radically removes all manual microwave operation steps.
judge_comment: A robotic arm is radical but costly and complex, and it still doesn't address setting the cook program.

title: Conveyor Belt Reheat
new_elements: Slide-through conveyor (Food moves through a tunnel cavity.); Place-and-forget heating (No timer or door operation.)
rationale: Substitutes cavity loading with a conveyor that requires no settings.
judge_comment: A conveyor tunnel is a real, radical zero-learning approach, but home use brings problems with variable foods, leakage, and size, and the settings problem remains unsolved.

title: Single-Serving Pod Microwave
new_elements: Sealed meal pod slot (Accepts only pre-coded pods.); Pod automatically cooks (Pod dictates time and power.)
rationale: Removes all user choices by using a closed pod ecosystem.
judge_comment: Pod-coded cooking removes all choices, though it limits what can be cooked and is similar to existing coded-package ideas.

title: No-Display Microwave
new_elements: Displayless face (No numbers, only a single light.); Reduces information load (Only on/off/ready states shown.)
rationale: Substitutes complex displays with absent complexity.
judge_comment: Easy to build, but removing the display does not by itself make operation simpler, and it leaves open how users set time.

title: Manually Wound Cook Timer
new_elements: Wind-up spring timer (Twist once; timer unwinds visually.); Analog one-twist timing (No digital precision required.)
rationale: The mechanical timer becomes a familiar egg-timer gesture.
judge_comment: The wind-up timer is familiar and intuitive, but it is essentially how old microwaves already worked.

title: Universal Symbol Knob
new_elements: ISO food-symbol knob (International food pictograms only.); Selects by universal icon (No language or numbers.)
rationale: Substitutes labels with globally recognizable food icons.
judge_comment: Pictograms help across languages, but food icons are ambiguous about time and power and are not very radical.

title: Magnetic Recipe Tiles
new_elements: Magnetic recipe tile reader (Place a tile on the door to load a program.); Physical preset selection (No menus or codes.)
rationale: Physical tiles make preset selection tangible and obvious.
judge_comment: Tactile tiles make preset selection obvious and are cheap to implement with NFC or magnets, with a fairly novel interaction.

title: Light-Guided Food Placement
new_elements: Projected placement outline (Light outlines where to put food.); Shows correct loading (No manual reading needed.)
rationale: Visual guidance removes learning about placement and orientation.
judge_comment: A projected outline is a fun addition, but it adds a part instead of substituting one, and food placement is not the main learning barrier (setting time and power is), so it serves the need only partly.

title: Auto-Centering Turntable
new_elements: Self-centering magnetic turntable (Food snaps to center automatically.); No placement skill (User cannot misplace food.)
rationale: Replaces the loose glass turntable with a self-aligning one.
judge_comment: It does substitute a component (the turntable), but centering barely affects ease of operation, and a magnetic turntable inside a microwave is questionable given the metal and the heat.

title: One-Touch Any-Food Button
new_elements: One-touch auto-cook button (Single oversized button that starts a complete cook cycle.); Infers power and time from food weight (Uses a load cell to choose power and duration automatically.)
rationale: Replaces the power knob and timer with one button, so the user learns nothing.
judge_comment: A single button is highly relevant, but weight alone is a weak proxy for the cook time and power a given food needs, and the idea is partly familiar.

title: Weight-Sensing Auto Power
new_elements: Load cell under turntable (Weighs food placed in the cavity.); Auto-selects heating power (Chooses duty cycle from detected mass.)
rationale: Removes the need to understand power levels for basic reheating.
judge_comment: A load cell is feasible and concrete, but the user still has to set a time, so it only partly removes the learning curve.

title: No Power Knob
new_elements: Fixed optimal duty cycle (Runs one tested power profile for most foods.)
rationale: Eliminates the five-step power knob and its learning curve.
judge_comment: Dropping the power knob is simple and cheap, but a single power profile will heat many foods badly and the idea is not radical.

title: Steam-Sensor Reheat Button
new_elements: Humidity sensor (Detects steam released by hot food.); Stops reheat automatically (Ends cycle when moisture spike indicates food is hot.)
rationale: Replaces time/power decisions with a single reheat action.
judge_comment: Steam-sensing reheat has existed in sensor-cook microwaves, but it directly removes time and power decisions and works well in practice.

title: Single Twist Timer with Auto Extend
new_elements: Spring-return 5-minute dial (One simple twist to start.); Auto-extends until food is hot (Adds time in small increments based on humidity.)
rationale: Keeps the familiar twist action but removes imprecise short-duration guessing.
judge_comment: It keeps the familiar twist and adds humidity-based auto-extension, which is practical and easy to use but only a modest change.

title: Voice Command Cook
new_elements: Offline voice recognition chip (Recognizes simple spoken cook commands without cloud.); Sets cook time by spoken number (User says a time and cooking starts.)
rationale: Replaces knobs and buttons with natural speech, requiring no interface learning.
judge_comment: Offline voice control removes the interface entirely and is plausible, though it is not very radical and noisy kitchens or accents could cause errors.

title: Barcode Scan-and-Cook
new_elements: Barcode scanner (Reads packaged food barcodes.); Reads package cooking instructions (Looks up or decodes time and power from the package.)
rationale: Removes the need to translate package instructions into knob settings.
judge_comment: Scanning a package is a clever way to skip translating instructions, but barcodes don't encode cook times, so it needs a large database and only works on packaged food.

title: Food-Icon Dial
new_elements: Pictogram dial (Dial marked only with food pictures, not numbers.); Maps food type to preset (Turns pictures into pre-tested cook programs.)
rationale: Substitutes abstract power/time with familiar food icons.
judge_comment: A pictogram dial is highly intuitive and simple to build, but similar preset-icon panels already exist, so it is not very radical.

title: One-Button Stop/Start
new_elements: Single momentary pushbutton (One button toggles cooking on and off.); Toggles cook cycle (No separate start, stop, or reset controls.)
rationale: Simplifies the control panel to one obvious action.
judge_comment: One button is simple, but it gives no way to set time or power, so it either limits function or requires hidden behavior that must be learned.

title: Magnetic Door Instead of Button
new_elements: Magnetic door seal (Strong magnetic gasket holds door closed.); Holds door closed and signals closure (Magnet position sensed when door is shut.)
rationale: Eliminates the push-release button and its mechanical learning curve.
judge_comment: A magnetic door swaps out the release button, but it barely affects cooking operation, and magnets near a microwave and the safety interlock requirements make it questionable.

title: Touch-Free Capacitive Door Seal
new_elements: Capacitive door-presence film (Detects human proximity and door closure without switches.); Detects closure without microswitches (Replaces mechanical interlock sensing.)
rationale: Removes moving interlock switches so the door simply works without special operation.
judge_comment: Capacitive sensing is novel, but it's unreliable as a safety interlock (and safety standards require redundant interlocks), and users see no operational benefit.

title: Hall-Effect Interlock
new_elements: Hall sensor and magnet (Non-contact door position sensor.); Replaces three microswitches (Provides safe door-open signal with one sensor.)
rationale: Simpler sensing means fewer mechanical failure modes and no user awareness of interlocks.
judge_comment: A Hall sensor is a plausible and cheap substitute for microswitches, but it's invisible to users and does little for ease of use.

title: Reed-Switch Door Latch
new_elements: Reed switch in latch (Sealed magnetic switch detects door hook.); Senses door closed (Replaces physical microswitch actuation.)
rationale: Makes door operation invisible to the user while keeping safety sensing.
judge_comment: A reed switch is feasible and concrete, but it is a minor internal swap with almost no effect on the learning curve.

title: No Door Button Push-to-Open
new_elements: Push-pull magnetic latch (Door opens by pulling, closes by pushing.); Door opens with tug (No separate release button needed.)
rationale: Substitutes the door button with an intuitive push-pull door.
judge_comment: Pull-to-open and push-to-close doors remove the need to find a button, which is intuitive and mechanically simple, with such latches already in use.

title: Foot Pedal Door Release
new_elements: Foot pedal cable release (Mechanical pedal opens door hands-free.); Opens door hands-free (User steps on pedal instead of finding button.)
rationale: Replaces fumbling for a door button with a single obvious foot action.
judge_comment: A foot pedal is a radical and clear hands-free action, but it is awkward for countertop units and adds clutter and cost.

title: Voice-Announced Timer End
new_elements: Text-to-speech beeper (Speaks 'done' instead of ringing a bell.); Announces completion (Clear spoken status replaces ambiguous ding.)
rationale: Removes uncertainty about whether the bell meant done or error.
judge_comment: Easy and plausible, but it only clarifies the end signal and does not simplify operation, and it is not radical.

title: Color-Changing Done Window
new_elements: Thermochromic door film (Window changes color as cavity heats and cools.); Shows cooking state by color (Replaces interior lamp and timer interpretation.)
rationale: Gives status at a glance without learning displays or buttons.
judge_comment: Thermochromic door film is a novel idea, but door temperature poorly reflects food state, and the film does not replace controls or the lamp.

title: Transparent No-Lamp Door
new_elements: Transparent microwave-shielding film (See-through mesh replaces metal holes and lamp.); See inside without lamp (Ambient light is enough to view food.)
rationale: Removes a lamp and its maintenance while keeping visibility simple.
judge_comment: A transparent shielding mesh is plausible in principle and removes the lamp, but it does little for ease of operation.

title: OLED See-Through Door
new_elements: Transparent OLED display (Door becomes a display only when needed.); Shows food and cooking status (Overlays simple icons on the real view.)
rationale: Replaces separate controls and lamp with one obvious visual surface.
judge_comment: A transparent OLED door has heat and RF problems, and an overlay interface could add complexity rather than remove it.

title: Augmented Overlay Doneness
new_elements: AR camera overlay (Projects simple doneness cues onto the door.); Highlights hot spots (Shows where food is already hot.)
rationale: Tells the user what to do without any settings knowledge.
judge_comment: AR doneness cues are appealing, but detecting hot spots is hard and the idea adds components instead of substituting simpler parts.

title: LED Ring Instead of Lamp
new_elements: Microwave-safe LED ring (Low-voltage ring lights cavity evenly.); Lights cavity simply (No warm-up and no bulb replacement.)
rationale: Substitutes a fragile incandescent lamp with a maintenance-free light.
judge_comment: LED lighting is already common in microwaves and does little for operational simplicity; an LED inside the cavity also has to survive microwave exposure.

title: Electroluminescent Door Panel
new_elements: EL door panel (Whole door glows softly to illuminate food.); Uniform interior glow (No separate bulb or window holes.)
rationale: Lighting becomes part of the door, so there is nothing to operate.
judge_comment: An EL door panel is more unusual, but it would likely interfere with the door's microwave shielding and the view of the food, and it does not simplify operation.

title: No Turntable
new_elements: Mode stirrer (Passive rotating metal fan distributes microwaves.); Distributes microwaves (Removes need for rotating food plate.)
rationale: User can place any dish anywhere without aligning or cleaning a turntable.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers are proven and already used in many microwaves; removing the turntable makes loading and cleaning easier, though it is not radical.

title: Rotating Antenna Instead of Turntable
new_elements: Rotating waveguide antenna (Antenna spins under the floor to sweep microwaves.); Even heating without plate (No turntable motor or glass plate needed.)
rationale: Removes the turntable as a user-facing object and task.
judge_comment: A rotating antenna under the floor is real technology used in flatbed microwaves, and it removes the turntable as a user concern.

title: Fixed Ceramic Turntable
new_elements: Stationary microwave-transparent tray (Fixed floor tray that never rotates.); Holds food without motor (Microwave stirrer does the moving instead.)
rationale: Simplifies loading because the tray never needs to be seated on a drive hub.
judge_comment: A fixed tray combined with a stirrer is plausible and simple to use, but it largely repeats idea 3.

title: Disposable Paper Tray
new_elements: Disposable microwave-safe liner (Paper or molded fiber tray used once.); No cleaning turntable (Food sits on a liner that is thrown away.)
rationale: Substitutes the glass turntable with a no-clean consumable.
judge_comment: Practical and easy to build, but a disposable liner is an obvious tweak that adds a consumable and does little for operating simplicity.

title: Piezo Shaking Plate
new_elements: Piezo vibration plate (Small vibrations move food during heating.); Moves food slightly (Replaces rotation with gentle agitation.)
rationale: Removes the visible turntable and its alignment while still improving evenness.
judge_comment: Piezo agitation is unconventional, but it's unlikely to move heavy food and it does little for the learning curve.

title: Steam Jet Stirring
new_elements: Pulsed steam jets (Tiny bursts of steam stir the food surface.); Stirs food without turntable (Replaces mechanical rotation.)
rationale: No turntable means no plate to place or clean, simplifying every use.
judge_comment: Very radical, but steam jets would make a mess, change the food and complicate the appliance, and the benefit to ease of use is unclear.

title: Self-Cleaning Mica Cover
new_elements: Hydrophobic ceramic waveguide cover (Splatter beads off and wipes clean.); Repels splatter (Keeps waveguide clean with no user action.)
rationale: Replaces a fragile mica sheet that can clog or need cleaning.
judge_comment: A hydrophobic ceramic cover is plausible and low-effort for the user, but it only affects maintenance, not operation.

title: Metal Mesh Waveguide Cover
new_elements: Stainless mesh cover (Durable mesh keeps splatter out of waveguide.); Keeps splatter from waveguide (Withstands scrubbing and never warps.)
rationale: Simpler maintenance because the cover does not degrade or require careful handling.
judge_comment: Metal mesh near the waveguide risks arcing and doesn't block splatter well, and it has nothing to do with operating simplicity.

title: Conductive Fabric Choke Seal
new_elements: Conductive fabric gasket (Flexible fabric seals microwave leakage around door.); Seals microwave leakage (Replaces rigid quarter-wave choke geometry.)
rationale: Door closes with less precision required, making operation feel simpler.
judge_comment: Conductive fabric gaskets are plausible, but the link to simpler operation is weak, since users already just close the door.

title: Lossy Ferrite Gasket
new_elements: Ferrite-loaded silicone gasket (Absorbs leaked microwaves instead of choking them.); Absorbs leakage (Tolerates imperfect door alignment.)
rationale: User does not need to close the door in a special way for safe operation.
judge_comment: Ferrite-loaded absorbing gaskets exist in RF engineering and are plausible, but they do little for user simplicity.

title: Magnetic Door Gasket
new_elements: Magnetic microwave gasket (Magnet pulls door shut and seals RF.); Seals and closes door (One motion closes and seals.)
rationale: Replaces careful latch alignment with a self-closing magnetic seal.
judge_comment: Magnetic door closure resembles refrigerator gaskets and gives a one-motion close, which is modestly useful, though magnets add safety and interlock issues.

title: Solid-State Inverter
new_elements: Solid-state HV inverter (Generates magnetron voltage without bulky doubler.); Drives magnetron without voltage doubler (Simplifies high-voltage section.)
rationale: Fewer high-voltage parts make the appliance more reliable and less intimidating.
judge_comment: Inverter technology already exists and is an internal change that doesn't affect user operation.

title: Smart Thermostat Chip
new_elements: Thermistor and MCU (Digital temperature sensing and cutoff.); Cuts power before overheat (Replaces bimetallic snap-disc guessing.)
rationale: Invisible safety means the user never has to manage overheating.
judge_comment: Digital thermal protection is feasible but invisible to the user, so it barely changes operational simplicity.

title: Shape-Memory Vent
new_elements: Shape-memory alloy vent (Opens automatically when hot.); Opens when hot (Passive thermal protection without electronics.)
rationale: Replaces a thermostat with a silent, automatic vent that requires no user action.
judge_comment: Passive thermal vent is mildly interesting but barely affects user operation, which is already hidden.

title: Auto-Discharge HV Circuit
new_elements: Auto-discharge bleeder (Drains high voltage immediately after shutdown.); Drains HV capacitor (Makes service safer without user knowledge.)
rationale: Safety is automatic, so there is no warning or special procedure for the user.
judge_comment: Bleeder resistors already exist in microwaves and have nothing to do with user learning curve.

title: Capacitor with Built-In Resistor
new_elements: Self-discharging HV capacitor (Integrated resistor safely drains charge.); Safe after unplug (No separate discharge step or label needed.)
rationale: Removes an invisible hazard and any service-related learning.
judge_comment: Service-safety component that is invisible to users, so it does not serve simple operation.

title: Thermal Fuse Instead of Thermostat
new_elements: One-shot thermal fuse (Permanently cuts power if overheating occurs.); Prevents overheat forever (No reset or user decision required.)
rationale: Substitutes a resettable mechanism with a fail-safe that users never interact with.
judge_comment: Thermal fuses are already standard, and a one-shot fuse worsens user experience if it blows.

title: Single Relay Interlock
new_elements: Safety relay (One relay replaces three microswitches.); Cuts power if door opens (Simple fail-safe door sensing.)
rationale: Fewer switches mean the door simply opens and closes without hidden complexity.
judge_comment: Replacing interlock switches with one relay reduces parts but removes redundancy and is not a safe substitution; it has little user-facing effect.

title: Mechanical Door Link Fuse
new_elements: Mechanical fuse link (If interlock welds, a link disables HV.); Disables HV if interlock welded (Passive backup safety without monitor switch.)
rationale: Reduces interlock complexity so normal operation stays obvious.
judge_comment: A passive safety backup is plausible, but it does almost nothing for operational simplicity or the learning curve.

title: Inductive Power Pad
new_elements: Inductive countertop power pad (Microwave receives power through a pad, no plug.); Powers microwave without plug (Just place the oven on the pad.)
rationale: Removes cord routing and plug fumbling from setup and use.
judge_comment: Inductive power at microwave wattage (1000 W+) is inefficient and costly, and removing a plug barely affects the learning curve.

title: USB-C PD for Low-Power Mode
new_elements: USB-C PD input (Runs low-power reheat from common cable.); Runs low-power reheat (Enables simple countertop use without main plug.)
rationale: Substitutes a specialized mains cord with a familiar cable for basic tasks.
judge_comment: USB-C PD tops out around 100-240 W, which is too little for meaningful heating, and it is only a power-input change rather than simpler operation.

title: Solar-Ready DC Input
new_elements: DC input (Accepts low-voltage DC from solar or battery.); Runs from battery (No mains cord needed in off-grid settings.)
rationale: Simplifies power connection to a single familiar DC plug for niche users.
judge_comment: A DC input is feasible with an inverter or DC magnetron driver, but it serves a niche and has little to do with ease of use.

title: Cordless Battery Microwave
new_elements: Swap battery pack (Removable battery powers microwave.); No cord (Place anywhere without outlet.)
rationale: Removes plug and cord management entirely for simple placement.
judge_comment: A battery pack cannot realistically sustain microwave power draw, and cordlessness does not address the need for simple operation.

title: Twist Egg-Timer for Short Cook
new_elements: Spring egg-timer (Familiar 0-3 minute twist timer.); Counts down simply (Replaces imprecise mechanical 30-minute timer for short tasks.)
rationale: Uses a universally understood kitchen timer gesture for short reheats.
judge_comment: Familiar twist timer is easy to use, but microwaves have long used mechanical dials, so it is hardly radical.

title: Sand Timer Shutoff
new_elements: Sand timer mechanical cutoff (Sand timer physically trips power when empty.); Stops microwave when sand empties (No digital timing or buttons.)
rationale: Substitutes electronics with a visible, intuitive countdown.
judge_comment: A sand timer that trips the power is quirky and intuitive, though timing accuracy and the safety switch are problematic.

title: Single Reheat Button with Humidity Sensor
new_elements: Humidity sensor (Detects steam from reheating food.); Auto-stops reheat (Ends cycle when food is hot.)
rationale: One button does all reheating without power or time choices.
judge_comment: One-button reheat with a humidity sensor is highly simple and feasible, but sensor cooking already exists on the market.

title: Any-Food AI Camera
new_elements: Cavity camera and food recognition (Identifies food type and amount.); Selects cook program automatically (No user input beyond closing door.)
rationale: Removes all settings by letting the microwave decide what to do.
judge_comment: Camera food recognition removes all input, but it is costly and not a cheaper substitute, and recognition errors are likely.

title: Heat-to-Temperature Default
new_elements: Infrared temperature probe (Non-contact sensor reads food surface temperature.); Heats until food reaches 60 C (Single default target temperature replaces power levels.)
rationale: The user just presses start; the microwave stops when food is hot enough.
judge_comment: Press start and it stops at 60 C, which is simple, but surface-only IR readings give uneven results.

title: Single Cook Anything Button
new_elements: Single auto-cook button (One large button starts a sensor-driven cycle.); Weight plus humidity auto-program (Infers time and power from load and steam.); Auto-infers time and power (Removes all manual setting.)
rationale: A single button makes operation obvious with zero learning curve.
judge_comment: Perfectly serves zero-learning-curve, but one-button sensor cooking is a known concept and reliable weight/humidity inference for any food is hard.

title: Voice-Only Microwave
new_elements: Voice command microphone module (Listens for plain food names.); Offline wake-word recipe parser (Maps spoken words to cook programs.); Start cooking by spoken food name (No buttons or dials needed.)
rationale: Speech replaces knobs with a universally understood action.
judge_comment: Speaking a food name is intuitive and offline keyword recognition is feasible, though noise, accents, and the lack of any fallback control hurt it.

title: Barcode Meal Scanner
new_elements: Barcode scanner (Reads packaged-food barcodes.); Packaged-food cook-code database (Stores time and power per product.); Auto-set time and power from package (Scan and cook.)
rationale: Scanning is simpler than interpreting time and power settings.
judge_comment: Barcode scanning is feasible and concrete, but it only works for packaged foods and needs a database, so it doesn't cover all use.

title: Pictogram-Only Dial
new_elements: Pictogram-only rotary dial (Icons replace numbers and labels.); Select by food image (User turns to the matching picture.)
rationale: Pictures eliminate the need to learn power and time conventions.
judge_comment: Cheap and easy to build, but it is incremental and food images map ambiguously to time and power.

title: Toaster-Style Pull Lever
new_elements: Toaster-style pull lever (Push down to cook, pops up when done.); Single motion starts and latches cook cycle (One gesture replaces timer and door button.)
rationale: The toaster metaphor is already familiar and requires no instruction.
judge_comment: The toaster lever is a familiar metaphor and a fun substitution for the controls, but it still needs some way to set time or the cook duration.

title: Push-to-Open Drawer Microwave
new_elements: Push-push drawer cavity (Nudge to open, nudge to close.); Load and unload without door button (No latch button sequence.)
rationale: Drawer behavior is intuitive and removes the door-button learning step.
judge_comment: A push-push drawer is intuitive, but it only removes a minor door-button step and does not address the controls, which are the real learning curve.

title: Auto-Open Door on Finish
new_elements: Motorized auto-open door (Door gently opens at end.); Opens when done (No need to understand bell or button.)
rationale: The finished state is physically obvious without interpreting signals.
judge_comment: A motorized door is feasible and signals completion clearly, but it adds cost and complexity, and it doesn't simplify starting or setting the cook.

title: No Turntable, Rotating Field Stirrer
new_elements: Rotating mode stirrer antenna (Moves the microwave field instead of the food.); Even heating without user-placed turntable (No plate alignment or assembly.)
rationale: Eliminating turntable setup makes loading food a single obvious action.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers are already common and the turntable doesn't really cause a learning curve, so this barely helps the need.

title: Maglev Drop-In Turntable
new_elements: Maglev turntable platter (Floats and spins without coupler.); Drops in without coupler alignment (Any orientation works.)
rationale: No alignment ritual means users cannot assemble it incorrectly.
judge_comment: A maglev platter is novel, but it is hard to build inside a microwave and it targets a non-problem.

title: Transparent Door, No Bulb
new_elements: Transparent microwave-shielding panel (See-through RF-blocking material.); See food without lamp (Removes lamp replacement and switch.)
rationale: Nothing to learn about lamp behavior or replacement.
judge_comment: A transparent RF-blocking panel is already approximated by the metal mesh in current doors, and the lamp isn't a learning issue.

title: Camera and Door Screen
new_elements: Cavity camera and door display (Shows food on outside screen.); Shows food status on door (External display replaces peering through holes.)
rationale: Users see status without understanding window, lamp, or reflection.
judge_comment: A camera and door screen is novel but costly, and it only helps with viewing food status, not with operating the microwave.

title: Voice Announcer Instead of Bell
new_elements: Voice announcer (Speaks 'done' and what is ready.); Speaks done and food type (Plain-language feedback.)
rationale: Spoken feedback is understood without learning a ding pattern.
judge_comment: A voice announcer is easy to build and clear to users, but it only improves completion feedback and is not radical.

title: Cook-Until-Hot Sensor
new_elements: IR surface-temperature sensor (Measures food surface heat.); Stops when food is hot, no time entry (Doneness replaces duration.)
rationale: Users need only know they want hot food, not seconds or minutes.
judge_comment: Cooking until the food is hot removes time entry, which directly serves zero-learning operation, though IR surface sensing is imperfect.

title: One-Touch Defrost
new_elements: Frozen-food one-touch button (Single icon for frozen food.); Runs preset defrost (No power-level choice.)
rationale: Defrost becomes one clear press instead of a power-level concept.
judge_comment: A one-touch defrost button already exists on many microwaves, so it is simple and practical but not novel.

title: One-Touch Melt
new_elements: Melt-soften one-touch button (Dedicated butter/chocolate mode.); Runs preset low-power cycle (No user-set duty cycle.)
rationale: A specific task gets a specific button, removing power-level guesswork.
judge_comment: A dedicated melt button is easy to use and feasible, but it is an incremental preset and not radical.

title: Two-Button Reheat or Defrost
new_elements: Two-button control panel (Only Reheat and Defrost.); Only reheat or defrost choices (Binary decision.)
rationale: Two choices are faster to learn than any multi-knob interface.
judge_comment: Very easy to learn, but it is a simple reduction of controls rather than a radical idea, and it limits functionality.

title: Twist-Any-Amount Spring Timer
new_elements: Spring-return twist timer (Any twist starts a cycle.); Any twist starts; no numbers (Duration is implicit not read.)
rationale: Twisting anything is discoverable and requires no numeric understanding.
judge_comment: An intuitive twist control, but 'any twist starts' leaves the duration ambiguous and risks over- or under-heating.

title: Wave-to-Start Gesture
new_elements: Gesture sensor (Detects a hand wave.); Wave to start default reheat (No touch needed.)
rationale: A wave is a natural gesture and avoids control-panel learning entirely.
judge_comment: Wave-to-start is easy to use, though accidental triggers and the lack of feedback on what it will do are drawbacks.

title: Foot Pedal Open and Start
new_elements: Foot pedal (Press to open and start.); Hands-free open and start (Useful with full hands.)
rationale: A single foot action replaces separate open and timer steps.
judge_comment: A foot pedal is unusual and handy with full hands, but it does not really address settings and it creates safety and placement concerns.

title: RFID Meal Tag Cooking
new_elements: RFID reader (Reads meal tags.); Meal-tag cook profiles (Stores auto programs.); Auto-cook tagged meal (No settings entered.)
rationale: Tagged food cooks itself with no user programming.
judge_comment: Tags remove all settings for tagged food, but they depend on an ecosystem of tagged meals and are useless for untagged food.

title: NFC Tap Phone Program
new_elements: NFC tap reader (Reads phone tap.); Phone sends cook program (No microwave UI needed.)
rationale: Users already know how to tap a phone, bypassing appliance controls.
judge_comment: Tap-to-send is plausible, but it requires a phone and app, which adds a learning step and doesn't really simplify operation.

title: Post-Cook More Button
new_elements: More button (Adds 30 seconds after any cycle.); Adds 30s to auto cycle (Only fallback control.)
rationale: If food is not hot enough, one button simply adds heat.
judge_comment: It's very simple and easy to build, but it only covers the after-cook fallback case and is not radical.

title: E-Ink One-Line Prompt
new_elements: E-ink one-line display (Shows one instruction at a time.); Shows one instruction at a time (No menus or modes.)
rationale: A single prompt removes menu literacy and mode confusion.
judge_comment: A one-line e-ink prompt guides the user step by step, which helps, but it still relies on reading and following prompts.

title: Only a Cook Button
new_elements: Single Cook button (One control for everything.); Starts sensor-based cycle (No settings at all.)
rationale: If there is only one thing to press, there is nothing to learn.
judge_comment: A single Cook button gives a true no-learning-curve interface, though sensor-based cooking accuracy limits it.

title: Smart Plate Auto-Cook
new_elements: Smart microwave-safe plate (Communicates contents and weight.); RFID weight plate (Plate identifies meal.); Auto-cook based on plate contents (No user settings.)
rationale: Placing food on the plate is the only action required.
judge_comment: Smart plates that identify the meal remove all settings, but the cost, the need for a plate ecosystem, and food variety make it impractical.

title: Recipe-Coded Cookware
new_elements: Recipe-coded cookware (Pot or bowl carries cook code.); Microwave reads cookware code (Auto-sets cycle.)
rationale: Users put the right vessel in and the microwave does the rest.
judge_comment: Coded vessels make operation automatic, but they require dedicated cookware and the coding method is unspecified, and it only partly fits the SUBSTITUTE operator.

title: Load-Cell Auto Time
new_elements: Load-cell base (Weighs food automatically.); Estimates time from weight (No timer entry.)
rationale: Weight is sensed invisibly, so users never set time.
judge_comment: Weight-based auto time is plausible and removes timer entry, but it is an existing approach and weight alone does not capture food type.

title: Humidity-Sensor Auto Stop
new_elements: Humidity sensor (Detects steam release.); Stops when steam detected (Cooking ends at food signal.)
rationale: The microwave decides doneness instead of the user guessing time.
judge_comment: Humidity or steam sensors already exist in sensor-cook microwaves, so this is highly feasible and relevant but not novel.

title: Electronic Nose Done Detection
new_elements: Electronic nose (Sniffs aroma compounds.); Detects aroma and stops (Done by smell.)
rationale: A human-like done cue removes any need to set duration.
judge_comment: Smell-based doneness is a radical idea and intuitive, but reliable aroma detection in a microwave cavity is hard and food-dependent.

title: Popcorn Acoustic Auto-Stop
new_elements: Microphone listening for popping (Counts pop intervals.); Stops popcorn when pops slow (No popcorn button timing.)
rationale: A familiar sound cue automatically ends cooking.
judge_comment: Acoustic popcorn detection is concrete and workable, but it only serves one food, so its effect on the overall need is narrow.

title: Solid-State RF Module
new_elements: Solid-state RF module (Replaces magnetron and HV chain.); GaN RF power amplifier (Precise electronic power control.); Continuous precise power with no duty-cycle learning (Power is automatic.)
rationale: Precise automatic power removes the confusing on/off power-level concept.
judge_comment: Solid-state RF is a real substitution that enables automatic power control, but the user-facing simplicity benefit is indirect and the cost is high.

title: Auto Power Modulation
new_elements: Auto power modulation (Power follows food state.); Sensor-controlled RF power (Closed-loop power control.)
rationale: No power knob means one less concept for users to master.
judge_comment: Sensor-driven automatic power removes a concept for users and is plausible, but the description is vague and not very radical.

title: Food-Photo Dial
new_elements: Food-photo dial (Real meal photos as settings.); Select by picture (Turn to food photo.)
rationale: Photo recognition is faster than reading labels or numbers.
judge_comment: A photo dial replaces labels with pictures and is intuitive and easy to build, though it is limited to a fixed set of foods.

title: Three Emoji Buttons
new_elements: Emoji button pad (Drink, leftovers, frozen.); Press food emoji (Three universal choices.)
rationale: Emoji meanings are learned socially, not from a manual.
judge_comment: Three emoji buttons are very simple and cheap, but emoji interfaces are fairly obvious and cover few use cases.

title: Single Toaster Lever Control
new_elements: Single lever control (Push down to cook, pops up when done.); Push down to cook, pops up when done (One control for all.)
rationale: Toaster-like interaction is already familiar to almost everyone.
judge_comment: A toaster-style lever uses a familiar metaphor that needs no learning, but it needs automatic sensing to determine the cook time.

title: Transparent Conductive Window
new_elements: Transparent conductive oxide window (See-through RF shield.); ITO microwave shield (Blocks microwaves without holes.); See inside without holes or lamp (Unobstructed view.)
rationale: A clear view removes hole-mesh ambiguity and lamp reliance.
judge_comment: A transparent conductive shield is a real substitution, but a clear view only marginally reduces the learning curve and ITO attenuation at microwave frequencies is a concern.

title: Proximity-Open Door
new_elements: Proximity sensor door (Detects approaching hand.); Door opens when hand approaches (No button press.)
rationale: Automatic opening removes the need to locate a door button.
judge_comment: Auto-opening is plausible and removes one step, but unintended openings and mechanical cost make it only a partial answer to the need.

title: Kick-Open Drawer Latch
new_elements: Kick-open drawer latch (Tap with knee to open.); Open with knee when hands full (Hands-free access.)
rationale: A universally understood nudge opens the appliance.
judge_comment: Knee-open is a handy hands-free feature but does little for operation simplicity and risks accidental opening.

title: Magnetic Seal and Hall Interlock
new_elements: Magnetic seal and Hall interlock (Seals and senses door magnetically.); Door seals and cuts RF without moving latch (No mechanical latch.)
rationale: A magnetic seal closes like a refrigerator, needing no latch learning.
judge_comment: A magnetic seal is intuitive like a fridge door, but it is questionable as an RF seal and safety interlock.

title: Opaque Smart Door with Screen
new_elements: Opaque smart door with screen (Screen shows camera view.); Display food from camera (No window or lamp.)
rationale: Users watch a normal screen instead of understanding microwave windows.
judge_comment: A camera screen replaces the window, but it adds cost and complexity and does not simplify operation.

title: Auto-Close Door
new_elements: Spring auto-close door (Door closes itself.); Door closes itself (No need to push shut.)
rationale: Removing the close-door step makes operation more foolproof.
judge_comment: Feasible and simple, but it removes only one trivial step and is not radical or a real substitution that eases operation.

title: Doneness Dial Not Timer
new_elements: Doneness dial (Marks like warm, hot, boiling.); Select rare-medium-hot, not time (Outcome-based setting.)
rationale: Users choose a familiar outcome instead of learning seconds.
judge_comment: Substituting an outcome dial for a timer is intuitive and cheap, though the mapping from setting to food type and quantity is ambiguous.

title: Baby Milk One-Button
new_elements: Milk bottle button (Dedicated baby-milk mode.); Heats to safe drink temperature (No time or power setting.)
rationale: A common emotional task gets one trustworthy button.
judge_comment: A one-button baby-milk mode is simple, but it covers a narrow use case and safe heating is hard to guarantee without sensing.

title: Universal Leftovers Button
new_elements: Leftovers button (One button for a plate of leftovers.); Reheats any plate (Sensor decides cycle.)
rationale: The most common microwave task becomes a one-press action.
judge_comment: A sensor-driven leftovers button already exists in similar forms, but it serves the no-learning need for the most common task.

title: AR Door Glass Instructions
new_elements: AR-coated door glass (Overlays next action on glass.); Overlays next action (Guidance appears where user looks.)
rationale: In-context prompts remove any need to learn the interface.
judge_comment: Radical, but AR glass adds complexity and cost, contradicts the substitute-with-simpler operator, and is implausible in a microwave door.

title: Guided Light Ring
new_elements: LED light ring (Pulses to indicate turn, start, stop.); Pulses to show next action (Color and pulse guide user.)
rationale: A guiding light is understood faster than labels or icons.
judge_comment: A feasible light guide, but it only augments the existing controls and is not a radical substitution.

title: Press-Turn Single Knob
new_elements: Press-turn knob (Press for power, turn for time.); Press for power, turn for time (One physical control.)
rationale: Combining two knobs into one reduces interface complexity.
judge_comment: A simple, cheap and plausible substitution, but similar knobs already exist and it is not radical.

title: Recipe Card Slot
new_elements: Recipe card slot (Insert physical card.); Optical card reader (Reads cook program.); Insert card, auto cook (No settings entered.)
rationale: Inserting a card is a simple physical metaphor with no menu learning.
judge_comment: Insert-card cooking is intuitive and buildable with a cheap reader, though it needs a card ecosystem.

title: Meal-Kit QR Auto Cook
new_elements: QR reader (Scans meal-kit QR codes.); Scan meal kit, cook automatically (No time or power entry.)
rationale: Scanning a code is easier than translating cooking instructions into settings.
judge_comment: Scanning kit codes is workable and removes entry, but it only helps for supported meal kits.

title: Robot Arm Loads and Starts
new_elements: Countertop loading arm (Picks up plate and places it inside.); Vision-guided robot (Finds food and door.); Places food and starts cycle (No human operation.)
rationale: Automating placement and start removes the entire user learning burden.
judge_comment: It is radical and removes operation entirely, but it is costly, impractical and the opposite of cheaper or simpler.

title: One-Twist Cook
new_elements: Single spring-return rotary dial (One knob that sets time and automatically chooses power.); Sets time and auto power in one gesture (User only twists and releases.)
rationale: A single physical gesture replaces two knobs and all power-level learning.
judge_comment: A single spring-return twist that sets time and power is very simple to use, but the auto-power logic is vague and the idea is only moderately radical.

title: Food-Icon Dial
new_elements: Pictogram preset dial (Dial positions show food pictures instead of numbers.); Auto-selects power and time by food type (Turning to an icon runs a preset.)
rationale: Users pick a recognizable food picture instead of learning power levels.
judge_comment: A pictogram preset dial removes the need to learn power levels and is easy to build, though food-preset dials already exist.

title: Push-to-Open Magnetic Door
new_elements: Magnetic pull-open latch (Door opens by pulling anywhere on the edge; no separate button.); Single pull opens door and cuts power (Latch and interlock act together.)
rationale: Removing the separate release button makes opening self-evident.
judge_comment: Pull-to-open doors already exist and only simplify opening, which is a minor part of operation.

title: Foot-Pedal Door Release
